When you walk in, it is like you are in Mexico. This is a true Mexican food no Tex Mexing it.
If you see a long line, don’t get discouraged, their service is fast and efficient.
Keep in mind that their tortillas are huge, corn ones are three times the size of your normal street taco corn tortilla and flour ones are  also several times larger than your average ones.
They have two Al Pastor trompas spinning even on a Thursday evening.
Seating can be a challenge, however, most people don’t sit there for a long time.
And ultimately, amazingly flavorful tacos! They also have bottle Coke. Tacos are a bit on a pricier side, but when you see their size, it makes sense.

text.text:
Weekend getaway in Austin, went here for lunch.

Ambience - located in an alley, can be a little confusing to find.  Walk into an alley bar, go through a door, walk through a small seating area, around the corner to the kitchen where you wait in line to order and get your food.  Can be fun if you like hustle and bustle.  Energetic atmosphere, everybody working fast getting customers their food.  No table service, you order, you wait for your food, you try to find a place to sit.

Food - very tasty, we order 3 different ones just to try out the variety between the two of us, along with a side of chips and salsa.  The salsa is outstanding…probably the best flavor I’ve had in a long time. Our tacos were steak, chicken, and pork, all on homemade tortillas.  Very fresh tasting and tasty, but the meat was chopped fine, tough to hold together while you eat without it falling out the ends.

Enjoyed the lively atmosphere and great quick lunch.

Would I go there again…yes

Would I recommend…yes.

text.text:
The best way to describe this joint is as a taco reverse speakeasy. Go down an alleyway, enter a bar, and pass through a door with a tacos sign, and you’ll find a bustling taqueria that slings some of the best tacos in town. Tortillas are homemade, and pastor is cooked on a trompo. Don’t feel like a taco? You can also snag a quesadilla or tostada-like volcanes. There are several salsa options, and drinks include Mexican Cokes and horchata, among others.

We ended up getting two tacos (pastor and carne asada), a nopales quesadilla, and an order of chips and guac. At $5 to $6 a taco, this wasn’t cheap despite the no-frills surroundings, but it was well worth it. Everything looked and tasted fresh and smelled amazing. D/10 is known for its pastor, and it’s easy to see why. Served in strips rather than chunks, it boasts a crisp edge and a nice bit of pineapple flavor. However, the asada, the salsa crema, and even the chips are all stellar here.

While seating may be hard to come by, on food alone, Taqueria de Diez is a solid ten.

We bid farewell to Vespaio last night. Our server Daniel was the highlight of the meal. Witty, welcoming, kind and funny. He started there a year ago this month. I hope he lands at another wonderful restaurant where he can shine.

Food was beyond delicious and the company even better. A couple of footnotes from us being we've been here many times over the years - no white table clothes (which gives a soft touch) and it was exceptionally loud which we just don't recall that ever being. It was packed to the rim. But we had our little corner in paradise. And Daniel was super attentive and knew his stuff. Ask for him if you can!

We started with split a Caesar salad - and those homemade croutons! Do NOT leave one behind whatever you do!

We also split a delicious bottle of 2019 Bourdeaux.

Shared grilled broccoli, pecorino with our primi of:

TAGLIATELLE CON FUNGHI & 1/2 order of BUTTERNUT SQUASH PANSOTTI

I may try to slip in to the bar side for a final happy hour before officially saying arrivederci.

text.text:
We had a spontaneous date night on a Thursday and hit up Vespaio after our favorite mezcal bar “El Chapulin” next door recommended it. We didn’t have a reservation and were initially told we could snatch a seat at the bar as it is first come first serve. We waited about 5 minutes before realizing it wasn’t going to be available anytime soon. We went back to the host and asked if we could be put down on the list for the next available table. It was going to be a 2 hour wait but we were going to hit up some stores to kill some time. Just as we were walking out the door, the host called us back to let us know that a cocktail table next to the bar was just now available and that it was open seating and we would have a server. Of course we took it!

As soon as sat down, they brought us some water and two menus. It was a bit loud but we could still make conversation without feeling like we were yelling. We were just overhearing everyone else’s conversations. Our server checked in and made some suggestions.

We ordered a Caesar salad and calamari to start which came out quickly. They split the Caesar salad into two plates which was a nice touch. The calamari was delicious, although I wish it was a little more crispy as it would fall apart as you grabbed it. The Caesar salad was okay, not anything special as I’ve had better.

We shared a pizza for our first plate and the server had recommended the hot honey pizza which was so good! It is brick oven baked and full of flavor and perfectly crispy. We ended up splitting the lasagna and it is massive! It was deliciously cheesy and the marinara was so flavorful! We both almost finished it and that is how good it is!

I definitely recommend making a reservation to avoid the wait and the noisey bar area with very tight walking space. I felt like people would walk by about 2 inches away from us and that’s how tight it is but for the convenience of not waiting it was worth it. Parking is street parking on south Congress but we were lucky to have found one about 2 blocks away. We enjoyed the walk to and from the restaurant so it wasn’t a problem.

Overall we enjoyed our dinner date and were fulfilled, literally and figuratively! We highly recommend this spot!

We went to Two Hands for brunch on a Sunday.  It was busy, but not overcrowded, and we had a reservation!

We started with Crispy Brussels Spouts and they were defininitely a favorite and so delicious!  The tables on either side of us ordered the Brussels as well!

I had the Two Hander Burger and it was great.  Very good Montana Waygu beef!  It comes with shoestring style french fries that reminded me of my childhood and were so crisp and tasty (see picture!). We also had the Salmon Quinoa Bowl which is a tasty, healthy choice, salmon was terrific.
The Steak and Egg was quality.  The steak was slightly underseasoned but the French anchovy dressing more than made up for it!  The hashbrowns and egg were both great with it!  Lastly, we had the Smashed Avo Toast with smoked Salmon and it was wonderful.
Also recommend the Hot Vanilla Orange Blossom Latte and for dessert, the Banana Walnut Bread topped with Espresso Mascarpone, so decadent!

I live locally and have had much better service here before but this negative experience makes me feel uncomfortable returning or recommending to others.

Treated myself out for dinner and glad I chose Two Hands. I contemplated on getting the Steak and Frites ($35) but ended up getting the Two Hander Burger (Double Cheeseburger with fries for $20)  and 5 oz Steak ($15). Basically paid for the price of the Steak and Frites Combo, but got a bit more variety.

The double cheeseburger was delicious. The patty was a good portion. Not too thick but enough to make you full. I enjoyed the petite size  of the French fries, they were nice and crispy. The steak was absolutely amazing, and melted in my mouth. I highly recommend the side order of the 5 oz seared range Montana wagyu steak. It was absolutely worth it.

Friendly service and relaxing vibes. I’ll be back, give them a try!

It is in a trendy spot right on touristy South Congress, so I guess that can be justification for mark ups.

text.text:
My Absolute Favorite Spot in Austin – Beer, Kolaches, and Community!

Batch Craft Beer & Kolaches is hands down my favorite place in the city; I find myself coming here several times a week! It is incredibly family-friendly—you’ll always see parents relaxing with their kids or babies in the massive backyard. It’s the perfect spot to soak in the Austin weather and that uniquely chill "Austin vibe."

What sets Batch apart is their commitment to live music. With both indoor and outdoor stages, there is almost always something amazing happening. I recently caught a Tango performance there that was so authentic, I felt like I had been transported straight to Argentina! I also love that they support Anthropos Arts, a local nonprofit for music education, by hosting student performances once a month.

Beyond the atmosphere, the quality of their craft beer, coffee, and kolaches is consistently top-tier. It is rare to find a place that excels at all three while remaining so community-focused. Whether you’re a local or just visiting, this multifaceted gem is something you simply cannot miss. 10/10 for the food, the music, and the heart!

text.text:
Jeffrey’s has been a regular stop for us, and Easter brunch added a new dimension to an already well-established favorite.

Everything about the experience felt intentional. The brunch menu struck exactly the right balance, familiar enough to feel like a proper Sunday meal, but with enough creativity to keep every course interesting. Nothing felt forced or overwrought. Just confident, well-executed food.

The drinks program is equally impressive. Whether you’re going mimosas or something more creative, the bar delivers. And the desserts, genuinely divine. The kind that make you reconsider whether you actually needed to save room.

What elevates Jeffrey’s above the crowd, though, is the service. Impeccable is the right word. Attentive without hovering, knowledgeable without being precious. You feel like a guest, not a table to turn.
Austin has no shortage of places competing for “best in the city,” but Jeffrey’s has earned that conversation. We keep coming back for a reason, and Easter brunch only confirmed it.

Jeffrey’s was the highlight of Austin. I could honestly go every day.
The service is impeccable, the team is on point, and the whole experience feels elevated without trying too hard. The margarita is incredible, and the wine selection is outstanding—especially on Sundays when bottles are 50% off.
The steaks are unreal. The Wagyu New York strip was perfectly cooked, and the filet had amazing flavor. The mushrooms are a must‑order, and the fries are thick, crispy, and so good.
We started with the truffle deviled eggs, which were spot‑on and the perfect first bite.
The only miss for me was the desserts, which didn’t quite match how amazing the rest of the meal was.
Overall, Jeffrey’s delivers on every level and is a must‑visit.

text.text:
My last night in Austin was spent catching up with a girlfriend I hadn’t seen in six years, so it felt only fitting to celebrate the occasion at a legendary restaurant like Jeffrey’s, located in the charming Clarksville neighborhood. I had heard so many great things about Jeffrey’s, including its reputation as an Austin fine-dining staple since 1975. The restaurant strikes that rare balance of feeling cozy and intimate while still maintaining an undeniably upscale atmosphere. Colin was our server and he did an amazing job taking care of us throughout the evening. Shortly after we were seated, we were served complimentary bread with stracciatella cheese, which got me super excited. Stracciatella happens to be one of my favorite cheeses and it’s surprisingly hard to find so this was a treat. The bread was warm and perfect for scooping up the creamy, delicate cheese. Extra points to Jeffrey’s for offering this as a complimentary starter!

After that, we ordered the crispy fried oysters, which were recommended to me by one of the sushi chefs at Sushi by Scratch who mentioned she used to work at Jeffrey’s and insisted they were a must-order. They arrived golden and delicate with a light, crisp exterior and that briny, buttery oyster inside. Truly the perfect starter and just the right portion to begin the meal.

For our mains, we both opted for the Gulf Red Snapper. The dish arrived beautifully plated with a perfectly seared exterior. The fish was delicate, flaky, and cooked perfectly.

On the side we ordered the oak-grilled broccolini, which came out vibrant and slightly charred with a subtle smokiness. It paired well with the snapper and added a nice fresh balance to the meal.

They also have an excellent white wine selection, which complemented the seafood perfectly.

Overall, it was a wonderful experience and the perfect way to end my Austin trip. Jeffrey’s will definitely be a staple stop every time I visit Austin from now on.

Took a bite of her Longhorn on an Everything bagel with bacon and the seeds on the bagel were burnt and honestly the sandwich was nothing special. I got the pastrami hash on sesame and did not care much for it either - the hash was under-seasoned which may be bec pastrami is salty but there was too little pastrami and too much pickled jalapeno which just overpowered the whole sandwich. I honestly didn’t even check if there was cheese bec I didn’t taste it. Servers were extremely nice though, and efficiently worked through the wall-to-wall Saturday morning crowd. And it sure was packed (we probably waited 20+ mins) which also made for a loud and claustrophobic meal, so we took it to go instead.

If I ever return, I think I’ll just get a bagel and cream cheese bec the sandwiches were just sadly, a let down, especially for the $12/sandwich price tag. Lots of other breakfast and brunch places in town with far better food and value.

The best thing was the garlic bread - very flavorful; the garlic on top was surprisingly good - it was fully cooked, so there was no heartburn or sharp flavor and it almost kind of melted in the mouth.

We got drinks from the bar next-door. They were fun to try very experimental and Christmas flavored. Can’t say they were bad, but they weren’t to my taste.

Parking was not a hassle, but also was not easy. There is a small parking lot. There is also some side street parking and a lot across the street (where I guess one can park when that restaurant is closed).

text.text:
4.2 stars
First of all, be prepared to have patience as this place had a huge line on a Sunday night. The guy that was running the orders was super nice. He gave good recs and even gave us free beets (bc we are indecisive and were between tomatoes and beets for the $55 abbi dish). The food took around 9 minutes to come out for the salads, tomatoes, beets, and garlic bread. The salad was pretty good (italian salad) but was quite strange how there were just chunks of garlic tossed in there (like whole cloves). The beets were decent, but the tomatoes are much much better tbh. The garlic bread honestly needed a bit more love; it is quite overhyped. If only it were hotter when it came out, had butter, and  cheese (then it would be perfect!). The stars of the show came out after: pomodoro pasta (very good!), cacio e pepe (mid!), and the pesto pasta (so so fire!). The chicken in tomato sauce was actually insane (get it!!). It comes with two pieces for the duo plate thing. My friend ordered a carbonara and hated it. It was not good tbh; it had a weird cheese mixed in with it. Otherwise, my final plea to the creative staff: bring fettuccine alfredo in place of the cacio e pepe PLEASE! Also a bolognese pasta!! Love the people that work here and the ambience! Will come back.

text.text: I have tried pretty much every single taco joint in Austin and El Primo is by far the best I’ve had. Coming from San Antonio, I was really shocked to see how pricey the breakfast tacos are here in Austin in general, but the tacos at El Primo are so good that I don’t even care about the price. Plus, it’s still cheaper than most of the places I’ve tried (about 4.99/taco). Customer Service is always top tier, and I go there so frequently that they recognize my face at this point! I also love that you can order ahead online since they tend to get pretty busy (understandable!!). They’re also next door to an amazing coffee shop, so you can get some coffee while you wait for your tacos. Long story short - El Primo is amazing and you need to try it!

We will be back!

text.text:
Emmer & Rye exceeded all of my expectations.
From start to finish, the meal was memorable and beautifully executed.

Starters
The Johnny cakes were a fantastic way to begin the evening.

The sourdough bread with butter was unbelievably good—so much so that I genuinely wanted to buy a loaf to take home.

Salads & Pastas
The salad was wonderfully balanced with a variety of flavors and textures.

The Cacio e Pepe was cooked to perfection and had the ideal balance of cheese and pepper.

The Pappardelle was good, though a bit too rich for the table; the richness tended to overpower the dish.

Mains
The carnitas were unique and packed with flavor, especially in the sauce.

The smoked half chicken was a standout juicy, tender, and perfectly seasoned.

Desserts
Every dessert we tried was exceptional.

Service
The bottle of wine took a little longer than expected to arrive, but the outstanding service and food more than made up for it.

Our server, Felix, was truly amazing attentive, personable, and knowledgeable.

Overall I would definitely come back. Emmer & Rye delivered an impressive dining experience from beginning to end.

text.text:
Overall: 4.5/5 [Dine In]

The staff was welcoming, and the restaurant is dog friendly! We brought our friend's dogs to the outside patio, and the staff even brought out a water bowl for them which was sweet.

The food came out at a good pace. They recommend 7 plates for 3 people, but we only ordered 4 since we had a heavy lunch. If we had a bigger appetite, adding an extra pasta or protein would round out the meal nicely.

Smoked Gulf Oyster ($18): Four oysters served in a delicious pork and miso butter. I am not an oyster person, but this one completely won me over. The flavor is already perfect on its own, so the peach hot sauce on the side is entirely optional.

Johnny Cakes ($16): Six small corn cakes with an egg foam sauce. The cakes were a touch salty, but the egg foam rounded things out nicely.

Pappardelle ($24): Oh my goodness, the pappardelle was so bouncy and fresh that we were perfectly happy eating it on its own. That is not to say the smoked wagyu short rib was not equally enjoyable. The meat was tender and beautifully flavored.

Texas Akaushi Wagyu ($65): The wagyu leaned on the saltier side, though it may be intentional. What really shined were the beef tallow sweet potatoes in black garlic sauce and chimichurri. They were delicious on their own and did a wonderful job of balancing out the richness of the meat.

text.text:
BELIEVE THE HYPE! Ok, so first off, I do have to acknowledge that living in Austin means I have access to ridiculously delicious burgers (budget, casual, fancy or whatever you want, Austin has killer meat).
Back to NADC …I’ve been wanting to come here for over a year but for one reason or another, kept getting delayed.
I figure that coming now would be a good representation of what the place is like given the IG fame and reputation has already been shared.

They only serve one line of burger (and tbh this intentional choice makes 100% sense) except on special occasions such as SxSw, ACL etc.

Best and simplest way to describe the burger is this: in n out’s Double double on steroids!
So so freaking good. The fries are not comparable to any other place out there so get them too! Crispy, good quality potato, excellent texture and all done in beef tallow. Boom!
Staff was welcoming, friendly and helpful as a 1st timer.

Can’t wait to come back soon!

text.text:
If you’re anywhere near Austin, do yourself a favor and stop by NADC Burger.

I’ll be honest—I was skeptical at first. Dropping nearly $19 on a burger had me questioning the decision. But the second I took that first bite, it all made sense. This isn’t just a burger—it’s a proper burger. The flavor, the quality, the way everything comes together… it hits on every level.

The patty was cooked perfectly, the balance of toppings was dialed in, and you can tell they don’t cut corners. It’s one of those meals where halfway through you’re already thinking about when you’re coming back.

Even though I don’t live in Austin, this is absolutely a spot I’ll recommend to anyone heading there. It exceeded expectations in every way.

Bottom line: yeah, it’s pricey—but it’s worth every dollar.

I ordered several items and was disappointed with the food overall.

The Fried Chicken & Mac ($20) was bone-in, which I wasn’t expecting, and I wasn’t provided a knife. More concerning, the chicken appeared pink. When I brought this to the server’s attention, I was asked whether it was still okay to eat. Maybe it was, but I wasn’t willing to take that risk.

The Hot Roast Beef ($17.5) was described as tender roast beef with brisket debris gravy and horseradish sauce, but it came across more like ground beef. The sandwich itself was very wet, which made it unappealing.

The Potato Salad ($4) with buttermilk and herbs was good. The Onion Dip ($7) was fine. The Hushpuppies ($8) were just okay.

Overall, I was disappointed with the food. The Uptown Sports Club space itself looks great.

Some hits, but a few things that need tightening up.  Probably will not go back.

text.text: Great neighbourhood hangout spot. This was my first visit to the newly relocated Cenote on E. 7th St in downtown and a thoroughly enjoyable one. Bright and joyful decor and wall art coupled with friendly service, robust and flavourful coffee and healthy food selection. I had the avocado toast and a whole milk latte. Had to come back for a second cup. Only a small 15 minute parking lot in the back but plenty of cheap metered street parking on surrounding side streets off of E. 7th. Spacious multiple patios and pet friendly. Recommended!

text.text: I tried out the Toasty Badger with my wife for brunch. We really enjoyed the cozy atmosphere, tasty food, and friendly service. The hash browns and pancakes were absolutely delicious and the rectangle shape was a unique twist (for hash browns). The French toast was good…though a bit overdone. The portions are understandably on the smaller side, except the massive pancakes. It is very popular, so expect to wait. Overall, a great place for some brekky!

text.text:
Had brunch here with a friend of mine who was in town from San Antonio. I’ve always passed by this place and have seen a line out the door so thought we would try it since it seemed “slow” on a Tuesday. The seats inside are quite tight and so you can hear other conversations right next to you. It also seems like others are listening in on your convos so if that is an issue I would suggest sitting outside. The inside is decorated really cute but it’s cozy with limited amount of tables.

When I looked at the Google reviews, I craved the pancakes so that’s what I ended up ordering. I didn’t realize the pancakes only come alone so you have to order any sides à la carte. My friend ordered the turkey sandwich which she describes as “sweet and salty” and it comes with fries and a chocolate dip. My pancakes came out looking super light and I was concerned they weren’t fully cooked thoroughly but they actually were. I would rate the pancakes a 7/10. They have a nice texture but they are more on the salty side. Not my style for pancakes but to each their own. The bacon was nice and crispy.

Our server quickly attended us but also seemed to forget about us after we ordered. I had to ask another server for a coffee refill. The table next to us also had to take their cups by the bar to get our servers attention for refills. She did come out with their refills and was apologetic. It might’ve been a shift change and she was probably stuck doing side work.

I would say it does seem overpriced for the value and quantity you get. Parking is tough and my friend had to park down the street by Wells Fargo. I might bring my husband here to try it out but probably won’t be our go-to spot. Especially if they have a long wait.

The coffee is smooth, well-crafted, and their Biscoff Latte Coffee is a standout, rich, sweet, and served with an actual Biscoff cookie on the side. The outdoor seating is spacious and relaxed, perfect for lingering with a book, catching up with friends, or just soaking in the Austin vibe. The atmosphere hits that sweet spot between lively and chill, never feeling overcrowded or rushed. If you're in Austin and want a coffee experience that's both tasty and inviting, this place is worth a stop.

text.text:
Yo! Coffee has become my Saturday and Sunday morning ritual, and I wouldn't have it any other way.

I'm usually here for a few hours — working, hosting my weekly meetup, or just soaking in the atmosphere — and every visit feels like coming home. Allie, Alexis, and Sarah are consistently warm, genuinely helpful, and the kind of faces that make you feel like a regular from day one. The mocha latte is my go-to and it never misses.

The space itself is something special. It's a converted house with an effortlessly cool vibe, a great outdoor patio, and an energy that's hard to manufacture — it's just there. They host trivia nights, bluegrass nights, movie nights, and rotating events that make this more than just a coffee shop. It's a community hub.

What I appreciate most is that it's a genuinely welcoming space. The signage isn't performative — it reflects the actual atmosphere inside. As someone who hosts a Sunday morning meetup here, that matters.

And if you haven't grabbed a taco from the Veracruz All Natural truck in the food truck area — fix that immediately.

If you want great coffee, good people, and a spot that actually has a soul — this is it.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Jacoby’s in Austin is an absolute gem! From the moment we arrived, the atmosphere was warm and inviting — rustic, laid-back, and perfectly Austin. The food was outstanding — every bite packed with fresh, farm-to-table flavor. I especially loved how the staff made us feel right at home, and the service was top-notch from start to finish.

What truly makes Jacoby’s stand out, though, is how pet-friendly they are. The patio is spacious, shaded, and welcoming for furry friends — our dogs were treated like family with water bowls and lots of attention from the staff. It’s rare to find a place that delivers both incredible food and such a relaxed, pet-friendly vibe.

Highly recommend Jacoby’s for anyone looking to enjoy amazing food, great service, and a place where your four-legged friends can join in on the fun. Can’t wait to go back! 🐾🍽️

text.text: Everything was wonderful! Portions were more than enough! Oh my goodness, if you like meatloaf you must try the BBQ Meatloaf! And the Parmesan Gnocchi is delectable too. The stuffed yeast rolls are tasty but filling so you only need one. My family members really, really, really enjoyed their Chicken Fried Chicken and Chicken Fried Steak. One of us had steak and based on his plate I am pretty sure he enjoyed it immensely since there was nothing left on his plate. And speaking of plates, I loved the plates that the food was served on because they reminded me of the dinnerware that we  would eat on at my Grandmother's house. The appetizer plates which were blue and white tins kind a gives a camping vibe. Loved the mason jars for water. We made reservations since there were 6 of us and we were seated in a nice area on the patio. If you happen to be fortunate to have Claire as your server you will be well taken care of. Oh one more thing, save room for dessert the strawberry cake is worth it.

text.text:
Overall: 4.1/5

Came on a Wednesday morning and there was no line so I got my order right away. None of the pastries had any strong or overwhelming flavors which I appreciated.

BBQ Pork Rib Kolache ($5.75): Delicious and probably my favorite of the three.

Churro and Dulce De Leche Star ($4.50): This was my least favorite. It tasted like a regular sugar donut with just a hint of churro flavor.

Horchata Donut ($4.85): Yum. It wasn't sweet and had a beautiful meringue on top. Just know the meringue will melt in the heat. The texture was softer than the churro and dulce de leche star which I preferred.

Pistachio Butter Latte ($8.75) + Oat Milk ($1.25): The cashier recommended this one and it was really unique. You need to stir it for a while since the butter on top is pretty thick. It wasn't sweet at first but as you keep sipping and stirring the sweetness from the pistachio starts coming through. I enjoyed it but it is heavier than your usual latte and I couldn't finish it all in one sitting.

COFFEE - Great! Quick. Exactly what we were looking for.

BAKERY - Fantastic! The cinnamon role was divine.

SERVICE - Speedy to a point of fault.

It’s okay to wait a bit - they 3 people taking orders for a line of 7ish people. They asked for our order before we could see the menu. This mentality of get people coffee as fast as humility possible made the space a bit cold.

If you’re expecting a nice experience with your barista and a cozy shop, look elsewhere. They are focused on speed.

If you’re looking for good coffee and appreciate speed - this shop is for you!

We really enjoyed the coffee at this place. The atmosphere is great, and it’s clearly very popular: we came for breakfast and it was quite busy. Despite that, the service was fast and well organized.

The food was excellent: all the dishes we tried were fresh, flavorful, and nicely prepared. Everything came out quickly, which was especially impressive given how many people were there.

The interior deserves a separate mention. It’s bright and welcoming, with large panoramic windows that let in a lot of natural light and make the space feel open and comfortable. Overall, it was a very pleasant breakfast experience: good coffee, delicious food, efficient service, and a relaxed, lively atmosphere that makes you want to come back.

Stopped into Proud Mary for the first time today and completely understand the hype. Had a great cappuccino along with the avocado, cilantro, egg, pesto & roti which was excellent.

What stood out most though was the level of care and thought behind everything going on here. You can tell this is a team that takes hospitality and craft seriously. Brandon took time to share more about the coffee program and what makes Proud Mary special, which made the experience even better.

Also appreciated Em and the team for taking care of me during a busy lunch rush. Looking forward to coming back and continuing to work my way through the coffee menu.

text.text:
No wonder this place is hard to get into! We snagged a last minute reservation on a day where temps were dropping in the evening, but were still able to enjoy their lovely patio with all the heat lamps.
Great wine based cocktails and a fun wine list. Loved the smoky drink especially and the orange wine from Chile 🧡🔥
We were recommended 3-5 dishes for 2 people and ended up ordering 5 because we couldn’t decide. At least something on the menu changes every 3 weeks, so won’t describe every dish. BUT, EVERYTHING that we ordered we would get again! It’s been a while since that has happened, especially in Austin. Just wow on all the flavors, textures and acidity balance.
Cannot wait to return and maybe get to the desert the time…the basque cheesecake has our name on it, but we were too full! Will just have to come back within 3 weeks!

text.text: One of our favorite places. We’ve dined here several times throughout the years and have enjoyed it very much. To celebrate life and also just because. The atmosphere is warm and cozy inside and the wine garden is nicely lit up. While I would say I am not typically a fan of a rotating menu, I thoroughly enjoy the change up here. (Although if I say so myself the squash, crawfish pasta, beef cheek with mushrooms, and honey pie are very missed!!! Bring back anytime! 😆) We did the tasting menu our very first time, but it works best for us to just order 4-5 things off the menu that we find interesting and unique. We always ask our server as well and we’ve never been misguided. The pullman bread is a classic that is always enjoyed every time. Crab fingers and hushpuppies are also menu staples that are good and seem to be available year round. We also enjoy the red wine selection they have. Most recently we had the roasted chili lime chicken and the sweet potato gnocchi which was great! We would 100% recommend and will be back.

My wife and I had a wonderful experience at Lenoir. We sat outside in the wine garden, which was absolutely beautiful — the large tree and the atmosphere made it feel really special and relaxing.

Our server, Ray, was fantastic. He was friendly, attentive, and made great recommendations throughout the evening. The food was excellent from start to finish. The Big Tree Oysters were incredibly fresh, the Black Drum fish was perfectly prepared, and the Half Chicken was one of the best we’ve had.

Overall it was a great dining experience with amazing food, a beautiful setting, and outstanding service from Ray. We would absolutely come back the next time we’re in Austin.

text.text:
This place is a South Austin gem. It’s thoughtfully tucked into an apartment complex, so you might miss it if you’re just driving by, but once you find it, you realize how special it is and why you see so many regulars in here. There’s an old-school Austin spirit, but it still feels completely modern and elevated in quality and taste.

I love sitting at the bar and writing. Everyone who works here is really cool and thoughtful, and the owners are truly good people. It kinda has a modern Cheers energy with creatives, business people, and apartment locals all crossing paths and talking to each other.

At night, the vibe shifts into a romantic spot for dinner and natural wine. It’s hard to find places that do all of this so well, especially in South Austin so I feel really lucky to have this spot in the neighborhood.

text.text:
We’ve been coming here since it opened and used to enjoy the drinks and food. However, we have been disappointed the last few times.

There’s always a lingering smell inside and every time we go all of our clothes will retain the smell. They need better ventilation in their cooking area which is right in the open by the cafe.

Today I went for brunch and ordered a mimosa. The mimosa was $13 and it was the smallest pour I’ve ever seen, with it being mostly orange juice. Before I drank any, I took a picture and asked the staff if this was the correct amount and they said it’s a 6oz pour. This doesn’t look like a 6oz pour, much less 6oz of wine. They dismissed my question pretty easily.

The prices are too high for the small portions. A similar thing can be seen in their matcha. While I enjoy the drinks, it’s one of the most expensive in town but one of the smallest. We really wanted to continue loving this place but the value is not there.

Food truck located with other food trucks in a shady area along the street.

Order taking was fast and efficient, I waited about 15 minutes for the food. My favorite part was the iced coffee which they kept cold as orders were prepared. Coffee tasted above average, very good coffee taste, surprising.

Breakfast sandwich was pretty good, I can’t say I fell in love with it, but it was a decent execution. I liked the compact presentation and the sausage. For me, the cheese was the weakest part, I prefer a natural tasting cheese vs the processed one used here.

Pleasant area to eat under the trees which provided shade on a very hot day when we were there.

Overall, recommended place if you are in the area.

P.S.: if this review was helpful, please leave a 👍, thank you 🙏

text.text: Hillside Farmacy has been on my list for quite some time and was finally able to visit…twice in 2 weeks because the food is that good! The owners Jade and Greg have done an excellent job of curating a delicious menu and transformed this old pharmacy into a cool atmosphere with the history of building still present. From the Farmacy Plate (meat and cheese board) and Arancini Balls as apps, I knew we were off to a great start!! For main courses, we ordered the Texas Wagyu Cheeseburger, Mushroom Pasta, and Steak Frites. My favorite of these was the mushroom pasta. I’m drooling again as I write this! Shoutout to Bird who is a fantastic server. She gave us great recommendations! Oh and I can’t forget the drinks! We ordered old fashioned drinks from the soda fountain, Hibiscus Lemonade and Turmeric Black Pepper on one trip and the Frozen Painkiller and Sandoval Daiquiri on the other. My words don’t do justice. You’ll just have to go and try it yourself. I have heard great things about their brunch too. I’d recommended getting reservations in advance because they fill up especially the patio on a nice day. Thanks Hillside Farmacy!!

Hillside Farmacy in Austin is such a charming little gem. From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere feels welcoming, cozy, and thoughtfully curated with that classic Austin character that makes you want to linger a little longer. The food was fresh, beautifully presented, and clearly made with care, but what really stood out to me was the overall experience.

Whether you’re meeting a friend for brunch, grabbing coffee, or simply looking for a relaxing place to enjoy a meal, this spot delivers. The staff was kind and attentive, the space itself is beautiful, and the entire restaurant has a calm, inviting energy that makes it easy to settle in and enjoy your time there.

text.text:
Food I had:

Swedish iced coffee & Smoked turkey Sandwich (no onion)

No hyperbole was used in writing this review.

When I took the first bite out of my smoked turkey sandwich, I thanked every god, of every religion, for allowing me to consume such a gift.

I’m not a big tomato guy. I’m not a big sandwich guy. This is no longer the case.

The Swedish hill smoked turkey sandwich has completely changed my view on what is possible regarding sandwiches.

The Swedish hill smoked turkey sandwich is a beautiful harmony of ingredients that does not care about you and your past. It will be the best sandwich you have ever had. It is the best sandwich. Period.

As far as the Swedish iced coffee goes.. this was an experience in it self. I am reviewing it apart from the sandwich.

This is peak iced coffee. I’ve only been on this planet for 23 years so maybe I’m not experienced to say this. But I believe this to be the pinnacle of coffee period. It actually tastes enough like coffee (somewhat bitter in the best way possible) but sweet (thanks to the oat milk and coconut cream). These two elements are combined in a way that allows the enjoyer the savor both sides, instead of simply having each part of the coffee combine and become one.

All of this to say, I had a great time. Please, if there is anything you do on your time on earth, try the Swedish hill smoked turkey sandwich and Swedish iced coffee. One have not fully lived until trying both.

JN

Ps I would’ve loved to wait a shorter amount of time for my order but I did go during peak times on a Saturday so I can’t complain.

On the other hand...the staff has never been warm or approachable. I try not to let that affect my experience, but it’s noticeable. Biggest downside was seeing espresso dispensed into a plastic cup as part of the drink making process before being mixed with syrup, milk, and ire. I’m used to seeing hot drinks mixed in stainless steel, so it made me a bit uneasy with what we know about microplastics and all.

My colleague finished her chicken biscuit and said it was yummy! She liked the spicy jalapeño sauce it comes with!

We were both fulfilled at the end of our meeting! I will definitely be back!! Highly recommend this spot!

We had an amazing Sunday lunch at Uchiba in Austin, and it was easily one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in the city. We made a reservation ahead of time, and everything from check-in to the final plate was seamless. The service was warm, attentive, and incredibly knowledgeable about the menu.

We ordered a variety of dishes, and every single one was standout. The Tiger Cry Bao was rich, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. The Ba Burger was surprisingly bold and packed with umami. The Donburi Chicken Thigh was comforting and deeply satisfying, while the Tokyo Shoyu Ramen had a clean, savory broth that felt refined yet familiar. The karaage was beautifully crispy and tender.

For sushi lovers, the Bluefin Otoro and Hamachi were melt-in-your-mouth perfection—fresh, buttery, and expertly prepared. We also enjoyed the Kankitsu sake, which paired wonderfully with everything we ordered.

text.text:
This review is primarily their lunch special. My partner got the $25 lunch prix fixe menu. We got a full sized Hama chili (iykyk) which immediately made the special worth it. Amazing cuts of hamachi paired with orange slices - this one always hits. For the main, we got the hot fried chicken which was decent. It was a bit overly saucey and salty but the chicken itself was juicy. The sorbet was peach and was a refreshing way to end the course.

I ordered the ba lunch with a burger ($38) which came with a sesame salad (delicious!), a handroll, and 2 nigiri pieces. The nigiri was sockeye salmon and akami; pretty basic but still very yummy. The burger was an American Wagyu - pretty standard but still very yummy :)

Lunch aside, Uchibā is one of my favorite sushi restaurants in Austin. Contrary to many opinions, I don’t think it’s “too expensive for what it is”, considering what the going rate for nigiri pieces a la cart is at other mediocre spots. I’ve spent birthdays here, celebrated my engagement, and just swung by casually whenever I had a sushi craving for consistent and delicious food.

text.text:
I had a good experience at Uchiba overall and enjoyed the food, though I wasn’t completely blown away. They do offer some solid vegan options, but the experience had a few drawbacks.

I was seated at the sushi bar, which I didn’t mind, but as a vegan it’s not exactly impressive to stare at a wall of refrigerated raw fish. It was also pretty loud, and sometimes hard to hear my server who was working behind the counter.

I started with a drink: the old fashioned with Japanese whiskey was light, delicate, and excellent. For food, the yucca chips appetizer was very good, and the eggplant bao was awesome (though not fully vegan). The menu created some confusion: the online menu clearly lists vegetarian/vegan options, the paper menu does not, and some dishes marked “vegan option available” apparently couldn’t be made vegan. That led to a slightly awkward ordering process.

From the sushi bar recommendations, I tried the watermelon nigiri, mushroom nigiri, and tofu avocado maki. Everything was good, but the mushroom nigiri was outstanding, possibly the best vegan sushi I’ve ever had. The tofu avocado maki, on the other hand, was a bit odd, with brown avocado that took away from the experience.

For dessert, I went with the strawberry sorbet. It leaned more toward shaved ice than sorbet, but it was creative and refreshing. Unfortunately, it took about 25 minutes to arrive.

Overall, a mixed but enjoyable visit. I’d definitely come back to explore more of the menu, but when it comes to vegan sushi specifically, I’d probably lean toward other spots in town.

I had a good experience at Uchiba overall and enjoyed the food, though I wasn’t completely blown away. They do offer some solid vegan options, but the experience had a few drawbacks.

I was seated at the sushi bar, which I didn’t mind, but as a vegan it’s not exactly impressive to stare at a wall of refrigerated raw fish. It was also pretty loud, and sometimes hard to hear my server who was working behind the counter.

I started with a drink: the old fashioned with Japanese whiskey was light, delicate, and excellent. For food, the yucca chips appetizer was very good, and the eggplant bao was awesome (though not fully vegan). The menu created some confusion: the online menu clearly lists vegetarian/vegan options, the paper menu does not, and some dishes marked “vegan option available” apparently couldn’t be made vegan. That led to a slightly awkward ordering process.

From the sushi bar recommendations, I tried the watermelon nigiri, mushroom nigiri, and tofu avocado maki. Everything was good, but the mushroom nigiri was outstanding, possibly the best vegan sushi I’ve ever had. The tofu avocado maki, on the other hand, was a bit odd, with brown avocado that took away from the experience.

For dessert, I went with the strawberry sorbet. It leaned more toward shaved ice than sorbet, but it was creative and refreshing. Unfortunately, it took about 25 minutes to arrive.

Overall, a mixed but enjoyable visit. I’d definitely come back to explore more of the menu, but when it comes to vegan sushi specifically, I’d probably lean toward other spots in town.

text.text: My partner and I tried to order to holiday omakase at home set for take out. We were told on the phone that because we were using a gift card, we had to go order in person (even though the website said we needed to call with a gift card). We waited about an hour for the take out. The omakase at home showed the “Ichi”box(a $95 value), with karage, brussel sprouts, and a pint of ice cream included. What we got was more aligned with their “Kaiso” box(a $65 value). So instead of 12 pieces of nigiri and two rolls, we received 4 pieces of nigiri, two of which were very browned avocado, then 6 pieces of sashimi and a single roll.

The red and green salsa were both great (I definitely preferred the green as it was slightly spicier, but both of them combined is the way to go)

For reference, I ordered the suadero, cachete, longaniza, and carnitas. I will definitely be back!

text.text:
This place has been on my list for over a year and last year I wasn’t able to stop by while visiting. About a week ago I listen to the chef/owner on the “she’s my cherry pie “ podcast and her passion and dedication to honoring her heritage and paying an affordable wage while being passionate about quality is impressive. $7.50 may be steep for a pastry but knowing the quality and effort that she puts into every item while paying affordable wages makes it understandable.

Anyway, This time it was a must visit on a quick over night trip.  I ended up not making it in till around 1230-1 so most stuff was gone but they had the seasonal strawberry sunflower seed concha which was what I wanted anyway.

The Concha had a nice crispy outside with a soft airy inside, the jam wasn’t too sweet and there was just enough sunflower to kiss your palate to let you know it was there.

I would have loved to try other items but what I did try was top notch. Hope to make it by again for more tasty treats soon.

text.text:
This is a very well-known bakery, and every time I’ve tried to visit before, they were completely sold out. I finally got lucky on a Sunday morning and managed to grab a few items.
The conchas are good, with a really nice crispy top. I preferred the vanilla one over the chocolate. The chocolatina is a beautifully glazed chocolate croissant and very flaky. That said, I found the chocolate in both the chocolatina and the chocolate concha to be surprisingly sour. You can tell they’re using high-quality, very dark chocolate, but the acidity was a bit unpleasant for me. I think it could use some balance. On the bright side, the sweetness level overall is just right.
The pink cake was my favorite item. The corn flavor really shines, and the texture is perfect. It was delicious and memorable.
Prices are similar to Rockman Bakery, so it’s on the pricier side, but the baked goods clearly have strong Mexican cultural influence, which I really appreciated. Overall, I’m glad I finally got to try it. Good experience, the chocolates are a little too sour.

text.text: We had a great experience here! My 3 & 6 yo daughters (and 3 mo son) and I went on a Friday night close to 5pm and the place was pretty empty (until about 20 minutes later). The atmosphere is so quaint and beautiful, the turfed field with a little tunnel, chalkboard, and sports balls was great for the littles, the snow cone place wasn't open but Besame and Veracruz were open til 8. From Veracruz we ordered the Al Pastor Taco, Grilled Fish Taco, and breakfast tacos (requested just bacon, egg & cheese) and they came out in a timely manner and were very tasty - the side sauces are a bit spicy but yum! From Besame we ordered the Mint Cookie Monster and some coffee flavored one I can't remember the name of and they were both delicious! Kind of pricey though, the kid size is $5.75 for like one scoop. The staff at both places were friendly and answered any questions. There is a bathroom located outside of the fenced area in the apartment complex, and parking is not great, although when we went we didn't have any issues. If we lived closer, we would definitely frequent this place more often!

Everything tasted great but they did get our order wrong. We had to go back up, pay more, and wait for the rest of the order. The patio is shaded and lovely to sit at with all the greenery. My kids had fun playing and there were lots of other kids and moms. My husband was actually the only guy there! We got a milkshake from Cookie Rich after lunch, and it was good but very rich; I guess they live up to their name! And that's coming from someone with a big sweet tooth. It was too heavy for one person to finish. They had a shave ice stand that wasn't open, so I'm not sure the hours on that. We definitely want to come back and try Goldy's next time!

Wow wow wow.  This place is truly a gem.  I know there are a million taco trucks in Austin, but this one is pretty special.

We stopped in and split a few different tacos: chicharron and egg, al pastor, migas, and chorizo/egg/cactus.  The chicharron was really tender and went well with the egg.  The pastor was crazy good.  It was shredded and had a lovely marinade and pineapple flavor.  The chorizo was fantastic because it wasn't super greasy.  Finally, the migas was super good and came with their homemade refried beans.  I'm pretty sure the tortillas were homemade or at least tasted like they were.  Their three salsas were really great too.

The older lady working the truck is so sweet.  She gave us great service and cooked up ridiculously good food.  It's like someone's little abuelita made us our meal. :)

We will 100% be returning for more.

BIG NOTE: The truck is cash only.

text.text:
I ended up going with the Pastrami Reuben as an appetizer, and I cannot lie. It was one of the best in the city.  The pastrami was sliced thin and generously stacked along with sauerkraut on grilled rye bread. However, tradition stops there because Swiss cheese is swapped out for pepperjack, and the dressing, normally a thousand island or Russian, is replaced with a beet 1,000 island sauce.

It is a sloppy sandwich and we ended up knife and forking it, but the goeyness of all those flavors melding together started the night out right.

There is not a lot of seafood on the menu here, that is not Dai Due's focus.  We did try the Gulf Brown Shrimp as an appetizer. Four large shrimp are skewered and served with charred tomatoes and a garlic vinaigrette.  My wife and I agreed we could have eaten three of those.

O.K. back to the meat.  When I previewed the menu, I focused in on their Cold Meat Board. It did not disappoint.  Wild Boar was the star of the show, presented in three different forms - a rillette, a pecan country pâté and a summer sausage.  A smoked duck breast and a chicken liver mousse with cherry mostarda rounded out the proteins on the board.  The dish was completed with pickles, Fireman's #4 mustard and an enormous mountain of grilled sprouted rye bread.

That's a lot to unpack!  The three wild board creations really showcased the talent of the kitchen.  I liked the pecan country pâté the best.  In the picture, it's the meat that looks like a slice of Spam. No, I am not comparing the taste to Spam, just the visual image.  The pecans do come through and with their buttery and slightly sweet taste mixing well with the rich, pork taste of the boar.  I liked to use the mustard on top of it too.  Definitely try it without the mustard first to see if you can taste all those flavors.  The boar summer sausage was equally tasty.  It had a slight, smokey, peppery flavor to it.  The rillette seemed a bit meh compared to the other items.  Maybe my taste buds were overwhelmed by the time I got to it.

While the wild boar was the featured meat, I felt the chicken liver mousse stole the show.  Mousse when done right has a smooth almost velvety mouth-feel, and yes it was done right.  Then the Dai Due kitchen topped the mousse with cherry mostarda, and the sweetness of the Italian condiment perfectly complimented the savoriness of the chicken.

I liked the mouse so much, I almost, forgot about one of my favorite charcuteries, the smoked duck breast.  The delicate cuts of smokey duck were shaved thin, and the taste, pure decadence!

A last note on the meat board, the bread.  So, I started off saying they served the meats with a mountain of bread.  Quite the opposite of many places that always seem to give you not nearly  enough crackers, crostinis or bread to get through the dish.  I laughed at first because it seemed like there was way too much.  Um, no.  As I got toward the end of the board I had to ration out the last two pieces.  Apparently, they know what they're doing -  like there was ever a doubt.

Their pudding is served in a small glass jar with whipped cream and candied pecans.  Even if you are full like I was, you can and should use this as an ending to your meal.  I also encourage you to try the Texas Valkyrie's Kiss which is a Wildflower Mead.

Overall it was a great experience at Dai Due.  I do not know what their other seasonal menus look like, but for what they have now, if you don't like meat this may not be your place.

I love the options, but know that going in meat is king at Dai Due.  Wonderful appetizers and sides, so like us, you can create a lighter meal if desired.

If you appreciate creative, fresh food that tastes incredible this is your place.  Service is impeccable.  What a gem for Austin.

text.text:
My husband and I decided to try out Dai Due for our 8th anniversary, and unsurprisingly it was amazing! First off the reservations were pretty open mid-week; I had booked for Tuesday several weeks ahead of time but then had some plans shift and was able to change my reservation to Wednesday just a couple days ahead of time with no issues.

We walked in through the front as the back entrance wasn't really obvious from the parking lot (which is quite small), but that was cool as we got to walk by the deli counter and see the meat and pickled veggies etc that were for sale.  Our server was great, very helpful in suggesting items, explaining the menu, and answering any questions we had.

On her suggestion we started with the sauteed mushroom appetizer but also requested the black garlic butter to be added on the side (I don't think there was an up charge) and this was a great choice! The mushrooms were tender but with a nice bite and super flavorful. We also got the grilled oysters- I forgot exactly what was in the sauce it had miso and something else, but it was so rich and flavorful!  I couldn't decide what was the best between the two apps they were both amazing.

The husband ordered the antelope over regular fries (as he doesn't like sweet potatoes) which they were happy to accommodate.  It was delicious- tender and perfectly cooked with the chive butter on top. I had never had antelope before and found it very pleasant, not very gamey but with a slightly different flavor than beef.  I got the quail over grits with a creole sauce and sauteed kale- amazing! It comes with two quail that I think were spatchcocked- the only bones were in the legs and wings so you could eat it easily.  The grits were creamy and the sauce with the kale and quail was delicious.  I was able to finish my whole meal but was pretty stuffed at the end!

Our waitress encouraged us to get a dessert but when we declined brought us out a bowl of chai ice cream to share as she said she wasn't going to let us leave on our anniversary without a treat!

All in all a great experience, only complaints are that they don't serve cocktails (there are plenty of local Texas liquors to choose from!) but we did enjoy a glass of wine, and then went next door to Vic and Als after dinner for a dessert cocktail!

I tried a few items from the menu and overall, it was a solid experience with a few standout bites. I ordered the brisket sweet potato, hummus and pita, and the pretzels with queso.

The hummus and pita and the pretzel with queso were both really enjoyable—fresh, flavorful, and easy crowd-pleasers. They felt well-executed and definitely worth ordering again.

The brisket sweet potato, however, was my least favorite. While it had potential, it ended up feeling a bit too heavy, and the texture leaned slightly greasy, which took away from the overall balance of the dish. I’d rate that one around a 5/10.

Overall, it’s a great spot for casual bites with some strong menu items, but I’d probably skip the sweet potato next time and stick to the appetizers that really delivered.

text.text:
We’ve been to Dish Society SEVERAL times now — for brunch, lunch, and happy hour — and every single visit always has some sort of hit!

The food here is fresh, local, and absolutely delicious, with so much care clearly put into every dish! The vibe inside is super cute, clean, and welcoming, with a small outdoor patio that’s perfect for a sunny Austin day and even if Austin's weird weather comes into play part of the outdoor seating is also covered.

When we've gone it’s never felt overly crowded (except one time during a morning rush, but we can see why) and the customer service has been phenomenal every time — from staff offering great recommendations to keeping tables spotless and making sure guests are happy.

We’ve loved everything we’ve tried, but a few standouts have been the Texas hot chicken sandwich (crispy, juicy, sweet, and savory perfection), the smoked salmon avocado toast (so fresh and flavorful), ranch-style eggs, and the grilled pesto chicken sandwich.

During happy hour, we grabbed the burger, some bites and drinks, with the burger for sure being a must — and the team even offered to cut the burger in half since we mentioned we were sharing. Small touches like that go a long way!

Their happy hour is also a great deal and definitely worth checking out. And if you’ve got a sweet tooth, don’t skip dessert — the Proud Pies they source from Houston are dangerously good. We still need to go back just to do a full pie tasting! The white chocolate pretzel bread pudding was warm, rich, and gave off total almond croissant vibes.

Oh, and don’t sleep on the mimosa flight — or their Mug Club, where you can purchase a YETI at their location and get free coffee refills when you bring it in. Genius!

All around, Dish Society is one of those rare spots that nails fresh, local food, great service, and good vibes every time. We highly recommend it! We'll be back, obviously!

text.text: When you think of a neighborhood place, this is it. It’s tucked away in the Rosedale community. Parking is sparse but once you overcome that, you walk into a Paris-like atmosphere. Quaint, quiet, small, bright, chic. I really love the vibe. The drinks were great. I got a coffee rum drink that was surprisingly clear (!!) and a vieux carre. They cost $18 each which is high. The food is also delicious but it’s pricey. The only complaint I have is that the biscuits came out very dark. While it was edible, I would’ve preferred if the waitstaff didn’t serve it and got another batch. We ate the entire plate of biscuits but the outside was slightly too crunchy. The pastry case is beautiful. It was definitely fun to go with my girlfriends ; I’ll have to try it with the family but maybe it’s too nice for little kids. I highly recommend this place for an intimate lunch or dinner!

Food: We ordered the trout tartare, French onion soup, fried shrimp po boy, and burger and frites for roughly $100.

-The trout was placed on delightful cracker with a generous serving of trout roe. It was rich with bursts of salt from the roe. I would just have added a bit of acid to round out the dish.

-The French onion soup had excellent flavor and the bread and cheese were perfectly baked on top of the soup. Exactly what you imagine when you think of a perfect French onion.

-The fried shrimp po boy has excellent. The breading was delicious, and the sauce took it over the top.

-the burger and frites was the only thing that I felt was truly lacking. It was just a bit too simple for me for 20. Maybe I’m being a bit too harsh though as I had previously had the best burger in my life while in Chicago at Au Cheval.

Vibes: This restaurant has such a charm from its interior down to its quaint location. We dined outside, but the inside was very cozy as well.

Service: FoH is very generous and polite. Enjoyed my interactions with everyone.

text.text:
Our visit to Nomade Restaurant was nothing short of exceptional—a true winner from start to finish.

From the moment we walked in, everything felt thoughtfully curated. The ambience is warm and inviting, with lush green plants surrounding the tables and soft lighting that creates a relaxed, almost transportive vibe. What made it even more special was the energy of the staff—every server seemed genuinely happy to welcome and serve, which added such a personal touch to the experience.

One of the biggest highlights for us was the menu. My husband was thrilled to discover an entire vegan selection with so many options—it’s rare to see that level of care and variety. And the food? Absolutely outstanding. The coconut flatbread was truly to die for—easily one of the best dishes we’ve had in a while.

Every plate we ordered was beautifully presented and packed with flavor. You could taste the attention to detail in each bite, making the entire meal feel elevated yet comforting.

An unforgettable dining experience that checks every box—ambience, service, and incredible food. Already looking forward to going back.

Very, very interesting decor, done in sort of a Mediterranean style.   I liked it, but the club music playing in the background seemed inapproriate for the vibe. It is quite open with little, if any closed off areas. We went on a chilly morning, yet the heaters took away any hint of the cold.

The waitstaff was very friendly, casually dressed and took pains to say nice things to us upon our departure.

We went for breakfast and had a carafe of French Press coffee which was bold and very smooth, 2 Wagyu Tacos and a gluten free waffle. The torillas were small, but each had so much on them, I could only eat one and they gladly packed thge other to go. I wish I had noticed it came with pickled onions. Aside from that, I really enjoyed it. One reason we came here from North of Austin is they are entirely gluten-free and my wife thoroughly enjoyed her waffle. It is offered with a nice fruit variety, but we requested just the kiwi for dietary reasons.

Overall, it was a good experience.

text.text: Worth a shot given all the great reviews, but we all left a bit disappointed. The food is decent, and I really appreciate that they don’t use seed oils, which more restaurants should follow. Unfortunately, we found all the dishes a bit too similar, and also a bit too familiar.  The barbacoa tacos for example - not particularly elevated in flavor. Only elevated in presentation and price.  The octopus was nicely charred but overcooked and too dry. The duck tostada was ok, with the duck lacking much flavor and the beans inside the tostada being too dry as well. The conchinita pibil enchiladas (they used a different name on the menu but they were definitely enchiladas) tasted like basic Tex mex you can get all over town for half the price. The yellowtail crudo was the best dish by far - and the only one that was actually a success. The churros for desert fell apart when you touched them. So, although we really wanted to like this, in the end we wouldn’t come back when you get a more flavorful meal at Torchy’s for 1/4 the price.

text.text:
We came to Summer on Music Lane for a date night, something my wife and I haven’t done in at least a year. My mom was in town, so we jumped at the chance for a night out. Overall, the experience was really great.

We started with the Ora King Salmon Crudo. It was good. I love capers, which is why I ordered the dish. The onions bring a strong flavor while the pear is more subtle, which balances everything nicely.

For our mains, we ordered the Squid Ink Orecchiette and the 44 Farms Strip Steak, with the Sweet Potato Papas Bravas as a side to share.

The Squid Ink Orecchiette was excellent and had a nice kick to it. I would definitely order it again.

The 44 Farms Strip Steak was ordered medium rare and cooked perfectly. The flavor was great, and it was paired with dressed arugula, which really brightened the dish and made for a great combination.

The Sweet Potato Papas Bravas were excellent as well. Soft on the inside with a great texture, and the butter had a really nice spice flavor that tied the dish together.

Our server also recommended a bottle of Duo, which was a nice pairing with the meal.

Service was great and the food was great. The only reason this ends up being a 4/5 instead of a 5 is a small detail, but one that stood out. As you can see in the photo, we were given a standard glass carafe for water instead of the green-tinted fish carafes that other tables had. It made our table feel a little less special and a little less coordinated overall.

We did ask if we could get one, but were told they had unfortunately run out. It may simply be that there aren’t enough for every table.

Small detail overall, but one that stood out during an otherwise really nice meal.

text.text:
Summer Moon has become one of my go-to spots for happy hour, mostly because of the outdoor seating and the consistently friendly service. The setting is relaxed and inviting — perfect for catching up or winding down.

That said, there are a few things to note. Wine isn’t included in the happy hour specials, which is a bit of a letdown. Also, I really miss the turkey sandwich — it used to be a standout, but it’s since been removed from the menu.

On a recent visit, I gave the burger a try but probably wouldn’t order it again. The pretzel bun and caramelized onions made it tough to keep everything together — more frustrating than enjoyable.

Still, the fries are great, and the atmosphere keeps me coming back. Just hoping the menu gets a few of those gems back.

text.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

The first time we visited The Well, we accidentally did the wrong thing — and honestly, I’m laughing about it now because the hostess told us it apparently happens all the time.

We walked into what we thought was the main entrance, ordered food on the takeout screen, and then proceeded over to the hostess stand… only to realize afterward that we should have entered through the other door. Once you get there, you’ll probably understand exactly what I mean. There’s definitely an opportunity for a larger “Main Entrance” sign or clearer direction at the front.

That small confusion aside, the rest of our experience was absolutely wonderful.

Every staff member we interacted with was warm, friendly, patient, and genuinely happy to help. The initial mix-up was quickly forgotten once we settled into a cozy booth with a great view of the restaurant.

The space itself is beautifully designed — modern, calming, thoughtfully decorated, and visually inviting without feeling overly trendy or forced. Everything feels intentional.

Then the food arrived.

Our dish was beautifully plated, incredibly fresh, and packed with flavor. What impressed us even more was learning how focused The Well is on creating a highly customizable, health-forward, and allergen-friendly dining experience. Nearly every dish can be made vegan, nut-free, dairy-free, or gluten-free.

Even more impressive, their menu is entirely free of:
• Gluten
• Dairy
• Seed oils
• Soy
• Refined sugar
• GMOs

We actually didn’t realize all of that going in, but after tasting the quality and thoughtfulness behind the food, we were seriously impressed.

The Well manages to create healthy food that still feels indulgent, satisfying, and beautifully crafted — which is not always easy to do.

We’ll absolutely be back and can’t wait to continue exploring more of the menu. Not pictured here, we also ordered one oat milk latte, and one Cortado— the coffee is also delicious.

text.text:
One of our favorite coffee shops in Austin, we've been coming here for about 5 years now.

The team is consistently fantastic, coffee is usually very good, and we love the selection of Sweet Bloom whole beans often available.

Really cannot speak highly enough of the team they have here. We've never had a single negative experience or even mediocre experience with the baristas here, they're really cool, great hospitality, answer questions, and again, cool as ice.

I hope the outdoor canopy can be replaced soon, also it's unfortunate how much seating is eaten up by customers from the bagel truck.

This is truly the best coffee shop in this part of Austin⭐️⭐️ ⭐️⭐️⭐️
The atmosphere here is absolutely lovely — warm, calm and beautifully curated in that effortless Austin way. I stopped by at the end of a long day, and their cappuccino was exactly what I needed. Rich flavor, perfect temperature, silky foam… it honestly brought me back to life.

And the cups?
The most Instagrammable cups in all of Texas.
The color is stunning — you just want to take a picture before you even take a sip.
I love it. 💛

Highly recommend this place if you want great coffee, great vibes, and a little moment of beauty in your day.

Iryna Nemova
ICF Certified Business & Life Coach (Houston)

text.text:
A coffee shop that has completely won my heart in Austin!
Stouthaus Coffee Sunset Valley is an absolute treasure and one of those rare places that gets everything exactly right. The coffee is consistently exceptional with a richness and depth of flavor that makes every cup a genuinely special experience. The baristas are passionate knowledgeable and take real pride in crafting each drink to perfection. The atmosphere is wonderfully inviting and relaxed making it the perfect place to slow down enjoy a great cup and recharge for the rest of the day. The space is always clean comfortable and filled with the kind of warm and genuine energy that only a truly great independent coffee shop can create. Stouthaus Coffee is without question one of the finest coffee experiences Austin has to offer and a place I return to time and again with great joy!

Drinks were good, and the staff was friendly and laid-back, which made the whole experience even better. It’s a great spot to go with friends, family, or even just to kick back by yourself for a bit.

Definitely a cool place with that Austin vibe. I’ll for sure be back.

This is my second time here during the week, and I love it! The old Victorian house is beautiful, and the vibes are great no matter what you're looking for. The upstairs is quiet and cozy, perfect for working remotely or just hanging outside to enjoy the weather and a nice drink. I got a coffee last time and it was great. This time I got a cocktail, and it was equally delicious.

ALSO, the owner (Harry with no hair) is great! Super friendly and provides great service. They also have events happening every night of the week: open mic on Mondays, trivia on Tuesdays, and karaoke on Wednesdays... so I will definitely be back to check those out! Highly recommend.

text.text:
Cosmic is one of my favorite places to hang out in Austin and a spot I recommend constantly. The atmosphere is unbeatable. Laid back, lively, yet relaxing all at once. It is the kind of place you can linger for hours without feeling rushed, whether you are meeting friends or just enjoying the space.

The drinks are fantastic and clearly fresh made, not syrupy or overly sweet. Great selection of tap beers & ales (please bring back the Moon Tower & the sour ales!!!) Everything feels thoughtfully done and intentional (like the herbs they use grown on site, chicken coop on site), which is harder to find than it should be. The food truck lineup is also excellent, with Wow Poke being the standout for me. Easily one of the best poke bowls around and the perfect pairing with a drink outside.

Great place to bring kids to let them get some wiggles out. I have met many mom friends that I still keep up with here! Cosmic nails the Austin vibe in the best way. Great atmosphere, great drinks, great food options, and consistently good energy. New redesign is awesome. An easy repeat and one of those places that makes Austin feel like Austin.

text.text:
Well well well….

I was a bit skeptical because the reviews are quite divided but let me tell you…go ahead and give this place a try. The biscuit sandwich was stellar, I LOVED the corn flavor that came through ever so slightly - don’t forget to try it with the hot sauce! The twinkies are nice IF you enjoy corn flavored desserts. They start off not too sweet but definitely get you on the backend after a second bite.

Customer service was pleasant! I was able to ask questions about the menu and didn’t feel like a menace lol.  It led me to trying the biscuit sando as I was told it was quite delicious. I’ll be back again. I can see why some wouldn’t like it - if you don’t like corn/masa in breads/pastries then maybe try a burrito. I’m always down to try modern twists on foods when it’s a merge of cultures.

Simple but effective and delicious menu. Not to mention I don’t feel like a glutton after eating the entire biscuit sando.

text.text:
Located in an alleyway, this place does some excellent Masa dough biscuits, yellow, blue corn, great coffee and a good filling burrito as well. The place has outside seating, service takes time as items are prepared with care and love, so give it some time.

The coffee I had, Platano flavored spiced coffee was wonderful, just wish it could have been more hot.

The biscuit jam has great refined flavors of corn, eat there then take out would be my suggestion.

text.text:
On a road trip through a little piece of Texas and found this spot. Overall rating pulled me in…I mean 4.7 that’s freaking great.

The guy taking are order was super friendly and helpful. We ordered the following items: Order horchata cold brew, PSL (coffee), Chile Colorado pork and added egg, biscuit sandwich and Mad Honey Bunny.

The horchata cold brew was extremely good. The PSL has a very unique taste didn’t hate it or love it. The biscuit sandwich was mid to be honest the sauce that is provided does not really add much to the sandwich. You won’t regret ordering it if that’s your thing. The mad honey bunny was not misleading but don’t go in thinking “better honey bun” it was a good solid spongy treat with a sweet salty tasty. The star of the breakfast is the chile Colorado and do yourself a favor and add the egg (not sure why that is extra and not a given) also the smokey flavored salsa on the side was an added bonus. I should have asked for more cause the little amount was not enough.

The seating was outdoors no indoor seating (I might have missed that when I was skimming)  and if you sit towards the back of the establishment it’s kinda near the major garbage so be advised you’ll get a fly or two or three.

It’s a nice pop in and grab something. Our meal was $45. I probably wouldn’t pop in again but it was a good breakfast spot. You won’t regret eating there.

text.text:
Prior to an event at the Long Center, we roamed across the river to the 2nd St District in sunny Austin for a bite.   My dinner choice of Gummie Bears at the Candy store was overruled...so we hit up Local Foods!  The vibe here is great with 2 levels of seating as well as outdoor and to go options.
Gal that took our order was efficient, friendly and helpful.  The Fall Dinner menu was exceptionally unique...I had the Gulf Seafood PoBoy with Apple/Cranberry salad and red potato salad for sides.   The potato salad is now my 2nd favorite, but will never surpass my #1 fave which is my dead Mom's specialty--just dont tell her!
The PoBoy was not the typical fake crab, small shrimp and an overload of mayo.  This was phenomenal.  The fresh dill in the potato salad took it up a notch.   My other half had a waygu beef sandwich with Mexican flavors.  Fantastic as well.  Too and we didnt save room for the brown butter miso cookies or carrot cake.   Great meal!  Now on to see Nick Offerman with a fully satisfied stomach......

text.text: We have walked by this place dozens of times, but we never really thought to try it out until this morning. We entered the space, and we were offered menus as soon as we walked through the door. The variety of main dishes and sides was ample. We were originally on the hunt for a breakfast sandwich, and we found so much more. The space is large and bright, and pretty busy - but not overwhelmingly so. We ordered at the counter, and took a seat toward the back. Our party of four had no trouble finding a table. The food took about 10 minutes to arrive, and it looked good before it even got to the table. Thumbs up all around for the Lil Nasty breakfast sandwich, breakfast plate, and the Avacado BLT w/ egg on sour dough. The avacado was freshly sliced and generous, tomato was cool and crisp, stacked lettuce leaves gave the sandwich excellent texture, and the bacon was crisp and hearty. The was kind of an afterthought...I really enjoyed it. The Hangover Potato's were really great, not sure what they did in terms of preparation, but they were unique in taste and texture. Very good. Also, one of my sides was sliced strawberries. Normally a ho-hum side, but this place upped the ante by including chopped basil with the strawberries - game changer! The whole experience was great and definitely going back next time I'm in Austin. Our only bother was the volume level of the music...seemed a little loud, but the general clientele were probably on their 20s and 30s, so probably more to their liking. If you are comfortable with a slightly quirky menu, then go for it! You won't be disappointed.

Alright let’s talk about Knuckle Sandwich at St. Elmo. I went. I ordered the namesake, The Knuckle Sandwich and very fortunately the guy didn’t punch me. Turns out it’s a punch for your tastebuds not the kind that leaves you needing an ice pack.

This thing comes out stacked like it’s been hitting the gym.   The way a dang good sandwich should be. Bread that actually holds together, meat piled up and needs a high pile permit, and all the fixings tucked in like they knew their role. Juicy, salty, tangy, crunchy, and a little bit of zing from the peppers. Dope.

Would love to have just posted a review with an empty plate (That’ll happen here.) because it was that good!

Have no fear of an Austin Knuckle Sandwich!
