text.text: After many, many, many 3-piece orders across all of their flavors and styles, it's high time to fully praise Nick and Cockti for their expertly and explosively delicious fried chicken.  Supremely crunchy, joyously juicy, and oh so well spiced, Cockti's fried chicken (thighs and legs) makes my stomach growl midday when I begin to think about having it for dinner!!  The spicy version is flavorfully hot, but not flaming, right where I like it!  The nuggets are equally amazing.  The extra crispy bits, cilantro, green onion and lime that is added in with each order makes for a delicious add-on. I can't speak to the sandwiches, though the huge bites being taken with closed eyes that I see when waiting for my orders tells me they must be glorious. I generally write in for their gluten free version, and happily wait the small amount of extra time it takes for Nick to make his magic happen.

text.text:
I live in Austin and have wanted to try this place for a long time, the owners are famous for being part of a local "taco mafia" with some other local taco places.

It took a while to order and get seated, plan to wait if it's a Friday night.

The food was good, my table shared chips and 3 dips. Tasty but kinda small portion. I had the duck carnita, very filling and rich. That was enough food for me. The fermented pineapple drink was my favorite part of the meal. My partner had the carrot tostada which we were told was not that spicy, but guess what, it was so spicy that's all you could taste.
The milk rice pudding dessert was super disappointing, way too sweet, rice wasn't fully cooked and again small portion.

Regarding the atmosphere- the place is very cool and laid back, the garden is a great touch, most of the seating is picknik tables or chairs with no backs. To get a table with chairs we had to sit closer to the speakers and the noise was way too loud. We all had to yell over the music to have a conversation, not my thing.

Overall the food was good but overpriced. This is a place for young Gen Z's who love standing in line for food, uncomfortable seating and overpaying.

text.text:
Had an amazing dining experience at Nixta Taqueria in Austin, a true fine-dine Mexican spot that exceeded expectations in every way. We were a group of three and ordered quite a variety — Beetroot Taco, Duck Taco, Tuna Tostada, and Chicken Taco — and every single dish was bursting with unique flavors and beautifully presented. The food was absolutely incredible — a solid 5/5 across the board.

The staff and service were exceptional, attentive without being intrusive, and clearly passionate about what they do. The vibe of the place was warm, modern, and energetic, creating the perfect atmosphere for a relaxed evening with friends. We also tried a few drinks, and they complemented the food perfectly — refreshing and well-balanced.

The only small challenge was finding parking, but once seated, everything else made up for it completely. It’s one of those places that makes you appreciate the artistry behind good food.

If you’re in Austin and want to experience elevated Mexican cuisine with a creative twist, Nixta Taqueria should definitely be on your list.

Must-try: Beetroot Taco & Tuna Tostada 🌮🍹

text.text:
I ordered the Super Burrito with steak (crispy), a Super Taco with carnitas, and chips with salsa. Overall, I thought the portions were generous and the prices were fair, especially for freshly made food.

As for the flavor, I would not call it bland like some other reviews have mentioned, although taste is obviously subjective. To me, the food leaned more on the mild side rather than being heavily seasoned. It was still enjoyable, but I do think the steak and carnitas could use a little more depth and boldness in flavor.

One thing that really stood out was the service. The ladies working there were incredibly friendly and welcoming, which made the whole experience even better. The food truck itself, along with the seating area, had a very warm, family-friendly vibe that made it a pleasant place to eat.

There was a bit of a wait, but it felt worth it because the food was made fresh. That said, if you are in a hurry, I would definitely recommend placing an online pickup order ahead of time.

I’d give this place 4.5 stars. The only reason I’m taking off half a star is because the meat portions felt a little lighter than I would have liked, and the steak and carnitas were somewhat too mild for my taste. I completely understand the realities of inflation and rising costs, but I’d honestly rather see a small price increase than a reduced meat portion. The food is still good, and I think customers would keep coming back.

There is a good amount of hype behind Asado’s so we expected some pretty good food going into it and what we got was something close but just a bit short. The lot Asado’s is in is nice with covered seating and other food trucks all around. They were pretty busy for a drizzly Saturday afternoon so ordering ahead was a good call for us. The food took probably 30 minutes or so between ordering to receiving the text it was really to pickup. They don’t have a pickup window as far as we could see so we waited on line and then grabbed our food at the front.

The food itself was good but not nearly what was expected in relation to its hype, something that feels a bit common in Austin. We ordered a carnitas super burrito and a cheese quesadilla. The super burrito came with the wrong meat, instead coming with chicken that had a bit of a dry and burnt flavor in it. Luckily that was masked by the rest of the burrito which did taste pretty good. The tortilla itself was soft but with a little bit of crisp to it that gave it a nice bite. Unfortunately, the cheese quesadilla was a miss. The tortilla on it was burnt and very crispy, which some may like, but is definitely not our preference. For what it’s worth, maybe this is just a style of Mexican food we don’t prefer but either way if you fall in line with that kind of flavor profile then maybe have a bit more realistic expectations coming into this place. Again, Asado’s is not bad, just not great. We’d suggest going for yourself and seeing if you’d agree.

came here for brunch and really enjoyed the atmosphere. the service was so lovely, and the upbeat mexican music added a lot to the good vibes. the fried plantains in the dishes were good, and i loved how spicy the salsa was!

the mole enchiladas were just alright for me, but i'm not a huge mole person to begin with. the migas poblanas taco was also pretty average in comparison to the other dishes.

overall, the food and ambiance were good, but the dishes were a little on the pricey side. probably wouldn't go out of my way to come back, but we definitely enjoyed the experience :)

text.text:
We first tried Loud Mouth at Austin Monthly’s Best Restaurants event last December and it was our FAVORITE bite of the whole night, so we had to make sure we checked out their spot to see if it held up.
Spoiler: it did!

The space is SO cute. It’s a renovated historic home with a big outdoor picnic seating area, plus indoor booths, tables, and a bar area inside the house. It’s one of those spots that works for date night, happy hour, or families (tons of room outside for kids to run around).

We went for happy hour (they have it DAILY, just check the times as weekend is different then weekday) and we also wanted to test out the inKind app. Everything worked seamlessly!

We asked to sit in the bar area and our bartender was awesome! She was friendly and attentive, even though she was the only one making drinks. She let me sample both frozen options (which were fabulous), and I ended up doing a half-and-half (per her suggestion) of the Creamsicle + Painkiller. Strong, smooth, easy to drink… dangerous in the best way! Honestly one of the best frozen's I've had and I'm not typically a frozen drink girl.

It was a little chilly in the bar area (and not just because of the frozen drinks ), but she even offered to turn up the heat. When our focaccia came out later than expected, she automatically comped it, which we appreciated.

Food highlights:
• Meatballs + Focaccia – Just as good as we remembered. Flavorful, comforting, and perfect for sharing. The bread is deliciously crispy, but you definitely need more then what it is served with to enjoy all the sauce.
• Italian Sandwich – The ROCKSTAR. Even though the bread was softer than we’d usually prefer for this style, it was loaded and packed with flavor. 1000% would eat this again!
• Joe’s Pie – Tasty, felt more Neapolitan style and had a good chew and flavor. Especially loved the mushrooms and olives on it!
• Warm seeded Focaccia – SO FLUFFY!

Overall, the atmosphere, service, and variety on the menu make this a spot we’ll absolutely keep coming back to. Loud Mouth lives up to the hype!

text.text:
We first went to Loudmouth about a year ago and just absolutely loved it. The Italian sandwich was beyond delicious and it came with these amazing thick cut homemade chips. We also loved the vibe, the decor, and the staff .. everything was great. Was a bit pricy but the food was so good, it felt worth it. We knew this would be a place we would come back to often.

Since then, we’ve been a bunch (somewhere between 6 - 10 times). Some of the dishes we’ve tried were the meatball app, the arancini, the meatball sub, and the kale caesar. All were good and things we ordered again in future visits.

Unfortunately, the food has been so different each time we go - the menu changes, the dishes themselves are made differently, and the portions seem to be getting smaller and smaller.

This past time the Italian sandwich was served on such small, thin bread, it seemed like about half the portion when comparing to the first time we went. I’m not sure if they ran out of the regular bread they normally use or if a thin French type loaf is what they’ve shifted too entirely, but either way it was disappointing.

They also no longer do the homemade chips (haven’t for a while - a few times ago they gave us bagged chips instead of homemade and now they don’t serve anything with the sandwich).

The prices have shifted too with some things a few dollars more and some a few dollars less than when we first went - because of that, no major increase with pricing (that we could see anyway) but for the current portion sizes, pricing is still a bit elevated.

Another big shift from this last visit was the arancini - we’ve ordered it several times and again, it was very good. It had a great sauce and plenty of it. This last time the dish hardly has any sauce though. While it did have a good crispy pancetta sprinkled on top, it was just inconsistent and lacking the flavor that the sauce brought to it previously.

Everything else - the vibe, staff, etc. - is still solid, but the inconsistency with the food, menu, and prices has made it hard to keep loving this place. It seems like they keep trying to switch something up - not sure if they are trying to solidify their dishes or if inflation / their distributors are impacting the dish switch ups, but too much change over a short period of time, especially when that change negatively impacts the dish, just isn’t a good thing.

Lastly, I’ll admit we have only gotten the pizza once here and it was okay but definitely not my favorite. Maybe it’s gotten better over time because it seems to be a favorite in other reviews. Perhaps this is just more of a place to go for pizza now vs. the other items on their menu…?

text.text:
I’ve been on the hunt for my New Orleans flavors right here in Austin, and thanks to the Frankie App, I stumbled across this spot and thought, “Why not go see?” Baby, I was not ready. I walked in and instantly felt like I’d stepped straight into the Bayou. The vibe hits you before you even sit down.

They greeted us at the door, and we barely waited to be seated. Indoor and outdoor seating are both available, and inside is spaced out just right—close enough to feel the energy, but not so close you’re sharing conversations with strangers. Menus are available by QR code or paper, whichever you prefer.

Our server, Claire, was a whole experience by herself—genuine, funny, honest, and fast. We ordered drinks (yes, Bourbon Street‑style and strong in all the right ways), and by the time I stood up to grab my glasses, those beauties were already on the table. Service here does not play.

The hardest part of the entire visit? Deciding what to order. The menu is stacked from top to bottom—drinks, appetizers, entrées, desserts, all of it.

We started with the Deviled Eggs and the Boudin Balls. Listen… there are no human words for how perfect those Boudin Balls were. Hot, crispy, flavorful—10/10. And if you dip them in that sauce, it takes them straight to an 11. The deviled eggs were creamy, savory, and topped with bacon—little pockets of joy.

For entrées, we had the Catfish Atchafalaya (a run‑don’t‑walk situation). I don’t even eat catfish, and I was tearing this dish up. I ordered the Chicken & Andouille Sausage Jambalaya, and baby, it had me dancing in my seat.

We wrapped it all up with their Gas Station Beignets. I told Claire whoever is back there making these must’ve gotten the recipe from Café Du Monde because they taste exactly the same. I’m honestly shocked there isn’t a line wrapped around the block for these alone.

This place is a 100/100 for me. If you love authentic Cajun cuisine, this is a must‑try. Austin, we’ve got a little slice of New Orleans hiding right here on East Ceasar Chavez.

Don’t be fooled because it’s in an old gas station this place has a fun atmosphere and great people that make the stop worthwhile.
We are definitely going back to try some of the other menu items and some of the special dates because every Tuesday is Fat Tuesday at the Lil Easy!

text.text:
Everything was so delicious. The chicken with the waffles was perfect, the waffle was premade witch I understand it easier and faster to do but the drizzle brought everything together and I have no complaints.

Gumbo and rice was great and was the perfect compliment to the chicken and waffles.

The Catfish atchafalaya really stole the show. It was everything I wanted and would have ordered that first but I didn't see it right away, not that I was rushed by the server, but I was hungry enough to to eat a cow.

Music is great, there is indoor and outdoor seating, and a bar I will have to try it next time.

text.text:
First time going to La Volta Pizza club was a success. Well, the second time. Don't make the mistake of going here on a busy weekend night without a reservation. It's going to take a while to get sat, which after eating here, I can see why this is a small little pizza shop. It doesn't have a lot of capacity. Came back on a Monday night with the reservation and it was smooth sailing.
Started off with an order of the meatballs. Amazing, great rich meatballs with a perfect sauce to balance it out. Then decide to share the hot girl pasta with the table. I will say this rigatoni alla vodka with sausage was a little bit spicy but we aren't the biggest spice people. Still it was delicious. Then the vodka pizza came out. We were a little scared that the vodka on the pizza would be just as spicy. It really didn't seem to be, the cheese balanced the vodka sauce very well and you couldn't notice the spice anymore. The crust on these pizzas is phenomenal. I think some of the best in Austin. Next we ordered the classic pie with extra sauce. That was a great and subtle difference compared to the vodka pie. Again, another all around amazing pizza. These pies are pretty dang big, you could definitely share one with three to four people. But there's no problem with leftover pizza for me. Great work guys

Edit: Lou's manager got my phone number from their self check out system and refunded me my Michelada. While that is nice and I will give them one more star for that, I will acknowledge how genuinely creepy and inappropriate that is to me. I can absolutely empathize that they are doing it to provide what they think is kind customer service. But to leave a negative review (not something I do very often) and get a call from them the next day actually freaked me out a bit. If they had replied to my review and asked me to contact them then that would've been a different situation. All this did though was actually convince me to NEVER go to a place that is requiring me to give my phone and email to check out for a tab again. Thanks Jenny!

text.text:
I’m from Vancouver and aburi oshi is a massive thing over there. It’s become popular among other big Canadian cities and I’m so freaking glad it has made its way to Austin :)!

The sushi scene in Vancouver is pretty big so let me know tell you this. Please ignore all the bad reviews Aburi oshi has gotten on Google so far. I see people upset about the wait but hell, it’s a soft opening and they’re trying to figure it out. I see people complaining that it’s just not good and hell, they probably don’t know good sushi lol.

The recipe, quality, and taste is the exact same that you’d get at Miku in Vancouver. I’ve ordered from their ghost kitchen multiple times and it has been consistent and tasty each time. My favorite is the salmon and ebi oshi sushi.

This has always been the one unique sushi dish I make all my American friends try when they visit Vancouver and they’ve always loved it. Excited for when they finally open an official location and expand further :)!

text.text: Second time at Birdies for date night. Went super early at 5 pm on a week night right before the snow storm and they didn't have a line out the door like usually. First time I was there they had a la carte ordering. This time it was a set menu and set price so be wary of the menu costing you a pretty penny but honestly with the food and service it was worth it. Great portions, delicious warm food, great presentation, and excellent service. So def worth the price!  Maybe bc it was a slow night for them but the staff was extra attentive, to a point where they were switching out plates faster than the entrees and items. Nicely done, wine 🍷 selection was extensive and expensive, worth it though if you are down to spend. Best part of the menu was the soup for me! So good I want to lick the bowl, We got the bread as extra, and paid the extra for the diff entrees so we could try both, less impressed by the entrees. On point for the dessert, both options were great. With the rotating menu I'm excited to come back and try something different next time. Keep up the good work Michelin all star team.

text.text:
They have limited reservations nightly but mainly do walk-ins, so if you can’t get reservations that doesn’t mean you’re out of luck. The line moves tragically slow even when they have tables open (I’ve yet to figure out why, but I’m sure there’s a reason). You place your initial drink order and modifications (if any) to the à la carte menu at the counter before being seated. If you don’t have reservations you pick your seating on the outdoor patio.

As noted, the menu is à la carte and changes monthly. They have a vast selection of beverages; they have more nonalcoholic beverages than most places and the selection is great.

The food is absolutely delicious and it’s quick to see how they earned their Michelin star. To date, the cabbage and evercrisp apple soup with chives is my favorite dish, but I’ve not had a single bad bite.

Everyone we have encountered seems genuinely happy to work there and offers excellent service.

The only unfortunate things about dining here are the parking (which is non existent - just get a ride share) and the acoustics. Everyone on the patio was shouting to be heard and it felt like the music kept getting louder as the diners did.

text.text:
This was the highlight of our trip to Austin and very likely the best meal of the year.
The menu is seasonal but very approachable. The staff is amazing, friendly and knowledgeable.
This is the type of restaurant that makes awards like the (well deserved) Michelin Star make sense to us monies.
We had their April 2026 menu. Everything was exquisite and delicate but very intentional. We had deviled eggs with pepper and trout roe, beet carpaccio, sweet onion tomato soup, caprese with ramps, sablefish and both of their desserts (pound Cake was my favorite).
Needless to say this is my best restaurant experience ever.

This restaurant is one of the best taco spots in Austin! You order at the counter, and the cashier was super nice. The restaurant has plenty of seating, and there was street parking nearby.

I loved the brisket taco! The tortilla had a nice, slightly crispy texture. The meat was extremely flavorful, and I loved it with the cheese. I also liked that there was a little bar with all the sauces. The green sauce was super good and not too spicy.

Paprika is phenomenal! Absolutely mouthwatering tacos.

Located on North Lamar, Paprika serves authentic tacos that will absolutely hit your soul. They serve five flavors on any given day, and have Al Pastor on Saturdays. The service here is very friendly, you are greeted as you enter and leave the establishment. Very cozy and welcoming environment.

I ordered a total of six tacos (3x Suadero, 1x Suadero Quesi-Taco, 1x Carnitas, and 1x Campechano Taco). They were all absolutely mouthwatering tacos-watering and delicious. The hot sauce here packs a punch, I was definitely sweating after a few bites!

Highly recommend this spot for my fellow taco-enthusiasts!

text.text:
Heard great reviews online about this place so had to check it out.
I will say these are THE BEST tacos I’ve had in Austin.

I got the bistec torta which was very good, the taste of the steak was very flavorful and a well put together torta in general. I also got the chicken tinga and suadero tacos, which I highly recommend. The tinga was the most flavorful chicken taco I’ve ever had and the suadero was really good as well.
If you’re between which beef taco to get (suadero or bistec) I’d personally choose the suadero.

My gf got a suadero, bistec and carnitas tacos. The carnitas was probably our least favorite of them all but still not bad.

**These aren’t street taco size, street tacos are usually on 3” tortillas and they use 5” tortillas**

We came very late in their hours (Austin traffic and they close at 6 pm) but the staff was very understanding and welcoming; everyone that worked there was so nice. They also informed us they have extended hours at a food truck at a nearby neighborhood bar (if I can find it I’ll come back to update my review).

The price: I want to say it’s more on the expensive side but unfortunately it’s just pretty on par with taco prices in Austin- BUT I will say the quality and flavor are there so these are actually worth it.

It was pretty dark when we arrived but it looked like limited parking.

Be prepared to spend $20+ per meal but also be prepared to have a party in your mouth because god damn the burger is good. I will definitely come back for more.

text.text:
We recently visited Sour Duck Market on a Friday evening and had about a 30-minute wait to be seated, which felt reasonable given how busy it was. The ambiance was great—laid-back, lively, and very kid- and pet-friendly, which we appreciated.

The food itself was tasty overall. The Wagyu burger was flavorful, though much smaller than I expected for the price. On the flip side, the focaccia melt was much larger than I pictured and very satisfying. We also tried the Jet Pilot frozen drink; it was definitely strong, with a heavy alcohol flavor that was a bit too much for our taste.

One thing to note is the dining experience is extremely hands-off. The hostess takes your name and seats you, and from there everything is done through a QR code—ordering, paying, and leaving. There’s no explanation of menu items, no refills offered, and no check-ins from staff once your food is delivered. If you prefer a no-interaction dining experience where you can just eat and go, this is definitely the place for you.

Overall, good food and a nice atmosphere—just know what to expect going in.

text.text: Popped in for some breakfast as my partner and I were headed out of Austin and im so glad we stopped through! My partner got the breakfast taco, it was so good she went back to order a second! I got the breakfast sammy and an order of fries with the most amazing ketchup (im assuming housemade) I've ever had. The breakfast tacos have a very layered but balanced flavor, the milder cheese option works better here. The breakfast sammy (sausage) was well seasoned - the fresh onion, arugula blend and cilantro avacado sauce were just that added touch of creamy, herby flavor. The fries were most definitely cooked in beef tallow and tossed in a zesty seasoning blend. We also got a cocktail and a tequila sunrise, both were delicious. The atmosphere was cozy and if I lived in Austin id go back for dinner and some cold beers on the spacious patio area. When im back in town, ill most certainly be visiting the restaurant again.

text.text: Second time here. Love love love their happy hour! 😍 3-6pm EVERY DAY! Got the single cheeseburger again, but couldn't recall if their special sauce was spicy, so got it on the side. Turbs out, it's slightly spicy and I accidentally put too much on my burger, so I think I'll skip the sauce entirely next time because I can't handle spice at all! 😅 I wish I had gotten the double since they are really thin smash patties but really good! Their fries are seasoned well but not crispy enough for me, so I skipped those this time with plans to get the ice cream for dessert. Unfortunately they didn't have any ice cream today, and said their ice cream machine has been out of commission for some time. I hope it'll be fixed the next time we visit, because their ice cream was amazing last time! I opted for the lemon pound cake instead (because they were already out of my first three  choices) and it was fine. Made me full and satisfied my sweet tooth, just wish it was a little easier to cut. But OMG their frozen dreamsicle margarita was indeed DREAMY! Like an orange julius and an extra strong margarita had a baby. lol Happy hour special are a cute, tiny size but two were enough to get me tipsy. Delish! Might get the regular size next time if they still have them. The citrus salt on the rim paired perfectly. 🤤

TL;DR: I went at happy hour and indeed was quite happy with everything! $6 burger, $6 drinks, good vibes. Will come back.

Food:
I went during happy hour, and I ordered a smash burger ($6), a paloma ($6), and an aperol spritz ($8). The burger is nothing extraordinary (just a patty and cheese), but it has a good flavor to it and is not greasy. I would totally order the paloma again: it has a nice subtle grapefruit flavor to it. Aperol spritz is a classic, but I would rather order another paloma!

Service:
You just scan a QR code to order, and you can open/close a tab easily. Love that it accepts Apple pay. Food came like 15 minutes before my drinks did, so there is definitely a bit of wait with drinks.

Ambiance:
I love the vibe out here -- it is essentially just a ton of benches with umbrellas to vibe at. A very chill outdoor experience, and all of my friends had positive things to say as well :)

text.text:
Overall Experience: This place truly exceeded expectations! The ambiance was warm and inviting, creating a perfect atmosphere for a great dining experience. The service was exceptional, with attentive staff making sure every detail was taken care of.

Starters: I began with the Duck Fat Fries—while they were solid and well-prepared, they didn’t quite stand out as much as I’d hoped. On the other hand, the Bone Marrow was an absolute highlight! Rich and flavorful, it paired beautifully with the fries, creating a satisfying combination that elevated the overall experience.

Main Course: For the main, I opted for the Korean Pork Belly. The dish was full of bold flavors, and it complemented the Black Walnut Old Fashioned perfectly. While the flavor was fantastic, I was expecting the pork belly to be more tender—it leaned a bit on the dry side. Nonetheless, it was still a delicious dish that I thoroughly enjoyed.

Final Thoughts: This place offers a fantastic dining experience with a perfect blend of great food, drink, and service. While there were a couple of minor expectations that weren’t fully met, I would definitely return for more. Highly recommend giving it a try!

Give Bufalina their Due! What an excellent experience all around.

The parking is a little tricky and there tends to be a little wait during happy hour, but trust me - it’s all worth it. This is high quality food made with expertise and love. Many of their major ingredients like the mozzarella cheese are made by a professional in-house and it absolutely shows.

The big stand-outs of our meal were the fried mozzarella and the vanilla ice cream. Yes - I did say vanilla ice cream. Don’t knock it until you try it. It’s also made in-house by a pro.

We also ordered the Talarico pizza and rigatoni pasta - everything was packed with flavor. The mozzarella started us out strong but the entrees still delivered.

We will definitely be coming back.

Excellent Happy Hour & Unique Small Plates
​We stopped in on a Friday afternoon for happy hour and had an incredible experience with our favorite server, Corinna. We decided to build a full dinner from the impressive and exotic appetizer menu—and it did not disappoint.
​We ordered the calamari, chicken liver mousse, mussels escabeche, spicy mushrooms, and the endive salad. Everything was fresh, delicious, and unique. We paired the meal with a bottle of Syrah, which was truly sublime. If you visit, ask for Corinna—her service is warm, enthusiastic, and incredibly knowledgeable. Highly recommended!

The service was pretty good, although not over the top and sort of transactional. Overall Rosie’s is a cute little restaurant to grab a drink or appetizers.

text.text:
Allday Pizza makes great pizza that's a half step short of excellent. Their fault isn't the taste, it's the execution, but that doesn't mean it loses a star. Hear me out.

First off, don't be intimidated by the line. There were probably 20 people in front of my date and I and we were ordering within 30 min having arrived at 615 pm on a Saturday. It moves fast. We were eating within 10 min of ordering. We got five unique slices of pizza, which means we nearly sampled the menu. Each slice is 1/6 of a pizza so ordering 6 slices is like getting a full pie.

Here's the thing, they perfectly cook their pizzas. The crusts are perfect, the char is perfect, the burnt tips of toppings are perfect. It's the best cooked pizza I've had in Austin. The issue is a combination of the pre made builds and thoughtfulness of what's on them. The spicy margarita slice should have more than one blob of cheese and a couple of basil slices. And work on that spice depth - figure out a better arabbiata, or let me know and I'll teach. The pep and pepp shouldn't have mountains of pepoerocini in some places and none in others. The arugula one is basically a salad. The best slice is the vodka sauce slice, but it's desperately missing a savory component which you need to add on.

It's so frustrating because everything here taste great, but knowing it could easily achieve excellence with a few basic touches is hard. At a minimum this is in the conversation for best pizza in Austin. At worst it's a disappointment because any thought into the food should lead a perceptive eater to finding clear gaps in it. Happy to return any time.

text.text:
We’ve eaten brunch here 3x now and it’s one of our favorite spots in Austin! Super cute inside and out with excellent service from the bar tenders to servers to chef. We’ve sat at the bar on one occasion, inside table another and outside (in the shade) and all have been great. Highly recommend reservations as it’s been busy every time we’ve been here.

I also appreciate that there’s onsite parking (free) and even though the main lot is often full, there’s extra spaces by the shops next door (all part of the same complex).

Now, onto the food… we’ve sampled a lot and the fall burrata is my fave. The avocado toast, migas, artichoke, and charcuterie board are also excellent. And of course, the pastries and chocolate chip cookies are a must try every time you come! Overall, prices are fair and portions are generous, we leave happy and full every time.

Highly recommend trying this spot out for a brunch date, girls get-together or even an adult birthday meal. If you have to wait for a table, go next door to Tiny’s milk and cookies and grab coffee and treats while you wait. Enjoy!

We will probably be back but might take some time to forget the sun par service.

Visited Elizabeth Street Café with a friend and had a really nice experience. The place itself is beautiful and cozy, and the staff was polite and welcoming, which made the visit even more enjoyable.

We ordered the Ginger-Chili Oil Dumplings, Spicy Chicken Crunch Spring Rolls, Mushroom & Tofu Bun, and Chicken Banh Mi. The Chicken Banh Mi and the Dumplings were absolutely amazing and full of flavor — easily the highlights of the meal. The Spring Rolls and Mushroom & Tofu Bun were decent but felt more on the average side compared to the standout dishes.

We also tried their French Toast, and it was excellent — perfectly cooked, flavorful, and definitely something I’d recommend trying.

Overall, Elizabeth Street Café offers a great combination of good food, pleasant ambience, and friendly service. I’d happily come back again, especially for the Banh Mi, Dumplings, and French Toast.

Must-try: Chicken Banh Mi, Ginger-Chili Oil Dumplings & French Toast

I stopped in for dinner today and ordered the fried shrimp bahn mi, and it completely blew me away. The shrimp was perfectly crispy on the outside, juicy and flavorful inside, with just the right amount of heat. The veggies, fresh herbs, and house-made mayo came together in the most delicious way on that soft, lightly toasted baguette. Every bite was an explosion of texture and flavor.
My waitress, Cassidy, was an absolute rockstar. She was super friendly, attentive, and genuinely enthusiastic about the menu. She gave great recommendations and checked on us at the perfect times without being overbearing. Her warm service made the whole meal feel extra special.
The vibe of the restaurant is charming and welcoming too. I’ll definitely be back soon — this place is a hidden gem! Highly recommend the fried shrimp bahn mi and asking for Cassidy if she’s working. 10/10!
Thank you Elizabeth Street Cafe and Cassidy! 🙌

text.text:
Elizabeth Street Cafe on South Lamar in Austin is a culinary delight, masterfully blending the sophistication of French cuisine with the bold flavors of Vietnamese heritage. The ambiance echoes this fusion, creating a unique and captivating atmosphere.

The Vietnamese wonton soup, a creative reinterpretation of the classic French onion soup, was a highlight of our visit. Rich, comforting, and perfectly suited to a chilly evening, it showcased the cafe's ability to reimagine familiar dishes with unexpected flair.

The Bahn Coun was a testament to the kitchen's skill, with tender, expertly cooked meat and a harmonious balance of textures and flavors. Each component was carefully crafted to elevate the dish as a whole.

Dessert was a symphony of refined indulgence: the macarons were delicate, nuanced confections, while the chocolate sesame puff was a sublime marriage of crispy, nutty, and rich elements, a true tour de force of textural contrast and flavor pairing.

Overall, Elizabeth Street Cafe delivers a distinctive and captivating dining experience, one that will appeal to adventurous palaters and those seeking a sophisticated take on traditional flavors.

text.text:
Beautiful place, full of tasteless food claiming to be Vietnamese 😕

Vietnam is known for its rich, yet light, aromatic umami food that brings complexity and depth while maintaining simple, light and refreshing. The food here really didn’t bring the flavors I know and love, being Vietnamese.

I’ve had Bánh mì far better out of trucks,
If you want to try Banh mi that is really Vietnamese, please got to Baguette House on North Lamar. Or Cơm Tấm Pa Phi.
Pho from Pho Dan is also a great pick.

The chicken Pho was underwhelming :( and very bland.
There was no Vietnamese pickled vegetables in my sandwhich. And if there was Pa Te I didn’t taste it.

It just makes me sad because to me Vietnamese food is so special, and they are boasting of having authentic Vietnamese food with Vietnamese names but just aren’t executing it and slandering what Vietnamese food really is. I’m assuming the good reviews are from people who don’t eat Vietnamese Food.

Despite appetizing visuals; the flavor didn’t suffice or measure up

I really appreciate the care he took with bringing me my food and making sure I was all set. The lemonade is fresh and so tasty—served in a sugar-rimmed glass. The wagyu tacos were fantastic, they look small but it was definitely plenty of food to be full on. Reminds me of a Barbacoa taco but less greasy and more delicious. The mole or salsa they bring with the chips at first is really tasty. Green one is spicy if you like spicy go for it! I mentioned that I was celebrating something and after my meal he brought me a slice of Tres Leches cake that was incredible! Excellent service, delicious food and a truly fun and unique experience. I love the decor like a fancy or elevated Low Rider theme and a perfect homage to Oaxaca, Mexico 🇲🇽 ❤️thank you for a wonderful and unique dining experience. It’s fun to people-watch in South Congress too. Plenty of parking in the lot or alongside the street.

A must visit in Austin, especially (but not only) if you love asian food.

My friend got the spicy chicken bowl, but did not enjoy it much and it was not spicy either. My friend also got the kimchi and said it tasted very authentic.
If you dine while seated on the back porch, you might see cute Uber Eats robots around for delivery pick up.

text.text:
Came here at 11:10 am on a Saturday and there was no line which was great! By the time we left at around 12-12:30 pm definitely already a long line forming, so definitely recommend coming when they open. Located in Hana Market (which unfortunately will close at end of 2025, but do not fear they are opening up a brick and mortar on Kramer) this ramen food stand is dishing out some seriously good food.

I am a vegetarian and I was worried there wouldn't be any items for me and was so happy there were two items on the menu I could eat and both were delicious! So glad they have vegetarian items - yes I know it shares a fryer but that doesn't bother me as I didn't taste any meaty flavors if that makes sense. The two dishes that can be made vegan/vegetarian is the mole tsukemen and their mushroom taco. I actually loved their mushroom taco more! The oyster mushrooms were smoky and seasoned well and I loved that the tortilla was half blue corn half yellow and had great soft texture without being gritty. Although at $9 my heart hurt for paying that much for a taco but it was delicious! The mole tsukemen includes the mole separate and it has a nice smoky flavor but definitely not sweet mole if you're thinking it will be like a chocolate mole flavor. The noodles were perfectly chewy and loved the roasted jalapeño that came with it. They didn't have their full menu available with shareables because I believe they are closing up shop but most of their menu was available.

Parking was super easy - free since it shares with Hana World. Also plenty of seating as they share with other food court restaurants so no worries about it being a tight squeeze.

text.text:
I loved how thoughtfully each item was cooked and how much effort clearly goes into every dish. The restaurant was packed, which says a lot.

The Jumping Fish ($18.50) came in a flavorful broth with plenty of fish pieces. The fish was perfectly cooked and delicately spiced — it literally melted in my mouth.

The Cumin Beef ($18.50) had a very interesting preparation; the beef was incredibly soft, moist, and buttery, not chewy or dry at all. Personally, I’m not a big fan of cumin beef as a dish, but the execution was excellent.

The  Sichuan Dry Stir-Fried Chicken ($15.99) was my favorite — deep-fried with the perfect crunch. Even after the drive home, it stayed crispy on the outside and juicy inside, never soggy.

My only downside was the spice level — even regular or medium was extremely spicy, with the cumin beef really burning my tongue. I’d strongly recommend ordering mild or least spicy if you want to fully enjoy the flavors. Every dish came with rice.

text.text:
House of Three Gorges is an absolute gem for anyone who truly appreciates authentic Sichuan cuisine. Sichuan flavors have a distinctive charm—bold, aromatic, layered with heat, and deeply satisfying—and this place delivers that experience beautifully every single time. As someone who is a big fan of Sichuan-style food, I’m always looking for restaurants that stay true to the cuisine rather than watering it down, and this spot does exactly that.
My buddies and I recently visited and shared several dishes, including the cumin lamb and the jumping fish, Sichuan dry fried chicken.. and all were outstanding. The cumin lamb was perfectly seasoned, tender, and packed with that signature smoky spice profile, while the jumping fish brought the classic numbing heat and complex flavors that Sichuan lovers crave. You can immediately tell the kitchen prioritizes authenticity and consistency—two things that keep us coming back.
The restaurant has built a strong reputation for delivering traditional flavors without compromise, and after multiple visits, I can confidently say the taste remains reliably excellent. If you enjoy real Sichuan cooking with depth, spice, and character, House of Three Gorges should absolutely be on your list.

Servers were attentive and the overall vibe of the restaurant was warming and inviting, and deservingly busy even on a Monday night.

Kome Sushi is hands down my absolute favorite sushi spot in Austin, TX. Simply incredible and will 100% be coming back!

I started with their pork gyoza, and it was incredible. Perfectly cooked, flavorful, and a great way to kick off the meal. For sushi, I went all in with four rolls and every one of them delivered. The Crunchy Dynamite roll with spicy tuna, avocado, tempura crunch, eel sauce, and sesame seeds had the perfect balance of heat and texture. The Alone Together roll was next level with tuna, salmon, and yellowtail topped with BBQ eel, go-go sauce, eel sauce, and tempura crunch. So rich and packed with flavor. The Summertime roll with spicy tuna, shrimp tempura, avocado, go-go sauce, and sesame seeds was fresh and satisfying. My last roll, the Midnight Sun, completely blew me away. Tempura fried with smoked salmon, cream cheese, avocado, candied jalapeño, sunflower seeds, and go-go sauce. Absolute perfection with the perfect sweet and spicy kick.

Everything was fresh, beautifully prepared, and bursting with flavor. If you love sushi and are in Austin, Kome Sushi is a must. I cannot recommend this place enough.

The Madison burger was honestly really good!! The pork belly patty was super juicy and packed with flavor and fat, but in a really enjoyable way. It almost melts as you eat it, and every bite has this smooth, rich wave of flavor with a slight sweetness that works really well. I do think the pork belly could have used a bit more salt, and maybe been a little more tender, but the caramelized onions and sauce help carry a lot of that and balance things out amazingly. It is a pretty unique and top tier burger - easy 9/10

The sweet potato fries were also great! Crispy, well seasoned, and just really solid overall. Definitely recommend getting them

One thing to note, they only take physical credit or debit cards, no digital payments so beware of that!

We were really looking forward to this experience, especially since it’s so hard to get a reservation but unfortunately, it didn’t live up to the hype.
We arrived about 15 minutes early for our 8:45 reservation and were seated quickly, which was a great start. However, once seated, the noise level was overwhelming. It was so loud that I could barely understand our waitress and unfortunately didn’t catch her name or most of what she said.
We started with the mozzarella sticks, which were actually very good but at $18, definitely on the pricey side.
For my entrée, I ordered the Lumache alla vodka. The sauce was delicious with a nice little kick, but the pasta itself was undercooked to the point that I couldn’t eat it. I ended up using my husband’s pasta just to enjoy the sauce. My husband ordered the chicken parmesan, which was decent, but nothing special especially for the price. The breading was soggy, and overall, we both agreed we’ve had much better for far less.
I don’t usually send food back, but in this case, it would have been warranted. Our waitress did stop by briefly a couple of times, but the interactions were very rushed more of a quick pass through than a check in so there wasn’t a real opportunity to address the issue. Given the price point, I would have expected more attentive service.
Overall, the experience didn’t justify the cost, and it was disappointing given the expectations. Unfortunately, we won’t be returning.
We did receive free ice cream for my husband’s birthday which was much appreciated and a good way to make us feel better about the evening.

text.text:
I’ve never been excited to write a restaurant review before, but Fonda San Miguel exceeded every expectation.

Located just off the main road in the Allandale neighborhood, the restaurant sits in an area where quiet residential streets mix naturally with local shops. We knew immediately we were in the right place when we saw cars making a beeline for the valet. The dramatic, old-world entrance—with its historic hacienda feel—set the tone instantly and had me genuinely excited for what was to come.

We arrived about 30 minutes early hoping to hang out at the bar, but the place was already buzzing and completely packed! We were told we’d be seated closer to our 8 p.m. reservation, which was understandable given how lively it was. The air was filled with conversation and energy. We made our way to the bar, but every seat was taken, always a good sign!

The bar itself is stunning. The back bar rises into glass-fronted shelves lined with vintage bottles, decanters, and colorful vessels, all dramatically backlit in saturated jewel tones. The bottles glow like artifacts. What truly elevates the space is the stained glass running beneath the shelving, so intricate, richly colored panels that cast a soft, prismatic glow across the bar top. Light reflects off the glassware and marble, creating a layered, luminous depth.

This restaurant nails every important detail from service and decor to food and drinks. Our server, Daniel, was phenomenal. His recommendations were spot-on, and he checked in at just the right moments without ever hovering.

What we ordered:

Appetizers

Lobster and Shrimp Tostada Special- one of the specials. A beautifully composed tostada topped with tender lobster and shrimp.
Queso Fundido with Rajas- arrived bubbling hot, rich, and comforting, with the roasted poblano strips adding just the right balance of smokiness and depth. What truly elevated it was that it came with fresh, house-made tortillas.
Angels on Horseback- beautifully executed, but what really stood out were the pickled vegetables served alongside the shrimp. Ate mine without the bacon.

Drinks

Pepino Pica (their cucumber margarita) — so good I had two
La Rubia- vibrant without being overly seeet
Paloma- clean citrusy and well executed. A classic drink you can never ho wrong with this.

Entrees

Vegetable Enchilada de Mole Poblano (my order): deeply comforting and beautifully executed. The mole was rich without being heavy, and every bite was savory and satisfying. One of my friends described it as perfectly authentic with an elevated flair.
Beef Wellington Special: ordered by my friend, who said it was cooked and prepared flawlessly.
Enchiladas Suizas: another solid, well-executed dish that was thoroughly enjoyed.

Dessert

Tres Leches (shared)- not your traditional overly sweet version. The flavors were beautifully balanced, light, and absolutely delicious.

A small but thoughtful detail: my friend ordered a Coca-Cola and it was served in an OG glass Coke bottle, which felt perfectly on brand. Shoutout to Paul, the manager, who made sure every table was taken care of and was consistently present throughout the evening.

Overall a 10/10 for ambiance, service, and food. Everything was top-notch. This is a must-visit in Austin, and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it to anyone!

text.text:
TLDR: Great for apps and drinks, not for mains. Service and seating left a lot to be desired — but there's enough here to give it another shot.

Visited 3/5/26 @ 8:30pm — reservation made a week in advance with a birthday note in the booking. They seated us directly in front of the hallway to the bathrooms and kitchen. Music blasting right above us. Our server had no idea we were celebrating anything. Not a great start.

The lump crab salad was a miss. Mostly thinly sliced cucumbers with scattered dollops of crab hiding in the crevices — my friend described it as cucumbers with tajin. Mint added freshness but it's not worth the price. The tuna tartare was good, slightly over sauced. The octopus was nicely cooked but there were only two small tentacles on the plate. Escargots were overcooked and tough, but garlic butter saves everything.

The mains were where it fell apart. The pork chop came out hot but was dry and almost inedible — the butter sauce and potatoes au gratin were the only saving grace, and the gratin was genuinely lovely. The steak frites was fine, cooked better than the pork, but tiny. We also waited a noticeable stretch for new utensils between courses.

Dessert redeemed things slightly. The mille-feuille had a beautifully thin, light pastry with vanilla cream that wasn't overly sweet. The fig sorbet didn't taste much like fig but was very pleasant regardless.

I'd still like to return as there were other items on the menu I wanted to try. Food also came out in a timely manner. The mains need refining.

Would recommend:
Potatoes au gratin
Mille-feuille
Get a table in the tent — too loud inside

Skip:
Lump crab salad
Pork chop
Tuna tartare
Escargots

text.text:
We visited Maie Day to celebrate my husband’s birthday after hearing great things about their prime rib brunch and wanted to finally give it a try.

When we arrived, there was a sweet birthday greeting card on the table, which was such a thoughtful touch to start things off. We had originally thought the prime rib was carved tableside (based on what we’d read before), but it actually comes pre-sliced and cooked from the back—which honestly makes sense for sustainability and consistency in the long run.

Our server was friendly, though not the most knowledgeable when it came to menu questions. Instead of checking on the answers, they mostly explained why they didn’t know, which left a few curiosities hanging.

Now for the food — the prime rib was absolutely delicious and hands down one of the best deals in Austin at $19 for a 10oz Wagyu. The cinnamon roll was flavorful with fun caramelized edges, but a bit more dense than we prefer (we’re team light and fluffy brioche). We also added eggs to our order, but they came out a bit after our steaks and sides — so the timing was a little off since we wanted to top everything together.

Toward the end, our check came before we were offered dessert, and only then did our server mention they meant to bring a complimentary birthday sorbet, which was a bit of a miss on the celebration experience.

Overall, we’d definitely come back for that prime rib, but the service and pacing made the visit feel a little less special than we’d hoped for a birthday brunch.

text.text:
Canje was just alright. The place is rowdy, the service is nice, and the staff's recommendation were pretty neat. But the food wasn't a complete home run.

The complementary pink pineapple was pretty good. I'm a fan of pineapple, so this starter was very refreshing. The sweetness, acidity, and spices melded brilliantly, making me devour the fruits quickly.

The Wagyu Beef Suya was easily the best thing I had. The presentation was cute, but the cook on the Wagyu was simply superb. It phenomenally seasoned and juicy, and the surrounding spices gave it a nice kick. The onions weren't too strong to make an impact and were pretty scarce (maybe make them pickled)?

The Wild Boar Pepperpot and Guyanese Roti came together. It makes sense because Rotis go well with a sauce, and it would be a waste to throw away the leftover Pepperpot sauce (apparently they use it to make their Cassareep Ice Cream). However the Pepperpot would've definitely matched better with the coconut rice because the sauce was quite sweet and not viscous. The Pepperpot is extremely similar to Szechuan Braised Pork Belly, so this dish had a very familiar, but welcoming feeling.

I was still hungry so I got the Jerk Beef Patties, but they were just over priced empanadas. I prefer the empanada to be gushing with flavor instead of having a dip. I wasn't impressed by the tastes and sizes, so I was pretty disappointed.

The Tres Leches was also just alright. I've had some pretty good ones, so I might have a preference in how they are prepared. The cake was light, airy, moist, sweet, and had notes of sourness from the seasonal jam. With all of that said, none of it fully delivered. I think the cake could've been at least 50% more sweeter, and the seasonal jam made the dessert more interesting/different instead of more tasty (to me at least).

Overall, I'm satisfied with the 5 dishes that I had and the price that I paid for. Although I had some good bites, I wouldn't give anything I had a strong recommendation. Do I regret coming here? No. Would I strongly suggest others to come here? Also no. I can see the appeal, but it wasn't for me.

Had dinner at Canje.  I had no expectations going into the restaurant, but was blown away.  We had four people and the waitress recommended 8 dishes.

We started with the Pink Pineapple, Jerk Beef Patties, and Wagyu Beef Suya.  All were delicious with the Pink Pineapple surprising the whole table. We finished with the Tres Leches and Stewed Mango Pudding.  Their take on the Tres Leches was a little different (not saturated in milk) but good.  The pudding was phenomenal!  I highly recommend and look forward to coming back.

text.text:
Rating: 3.8/5 [dine in]

Honestly an overpriced Japanese restaurant, and there are much better places in Austin. The small tapas-style plates for sharing add up quickly. We visited during happy hour with friends and also returned on a separate date night at regular pricing. Service is good and the ambiance is nice, but the food was just okay. I prefer Uchi or Uchiko over Tenten. The cocktails are also hit or miss. If you want to try this place, definitely go during happy hour.

During happy hour, we tried the Hamachi, King Salmon, Spicy Tuna, Negi Toro, and Scallop Makis ($10 HH), and the King Salmon was my favorite.

Kyoto Blush ($10 HH): A very sweet cocktail that tastes like it has no alcohol in it.

Fig Old Fashioned ($10): Better than the Kyoto Blush and not overpowering.

Sake Flight ($12): Comes with three 2 oz pours to sample - Nihon Sakari, Kiku Masamune, and Shiokawa Yamahai 'Cowboy'. I'm not a sake person, but think this is a great flight for beginners or for introducing someone to sake.

Charred Edamame ($8 HH): I didn't get to try it, but the whole table loved it.

Chicken Karaage ($8 HH): Good and worth ordering as an appetizer.

Goto's Sakura Martini ($17): Tastes almost like straight alcohol with nothing sweet or floral about it. I could not get through more than a few sips.

Yuzu Picanta ($17): Tequila, sake, pineapple, and yuzu. This tasted much better than the Goto's Sakura Martini.

Daikon Pork Belly ($14): Interesting and worth trying. The daikon balances out the richness of the pork belly nicely.

Wagyu Taco (2 for $24): Tiny, and reminded me of Toca Madera.

Miso Roasted Beets ($14): One of their seasonal specials. Good, but not as amazing as our waitress made it out to be.

My husband also had the A5 Wagyu Nigiri ($14), Uni Santa Barbara Nigiri ($11), Bluefin O-toro Nigiri ($12), Salmon Toro Nigiri ($5.50), and Hamachi Carpaccio ($28).

What a gem of a restaurant. Sitting at the counter we had a perfect view of the choreographed operations of the kitchen and got a masterclass in restaurant kitchen operations. Amazing to see all the orders getting cooked in that kitchen. Their wood fired oven is their center of operations and making me thing that I need one too:-).  Our seating at the counter also allowed us access to the Chef Chelsea who was such a gracious host and wonderful to speak to.

My burger was just awesome. The meat combination they used was well balanced and the fries were also perfectly crisp outside and soft inside. The starwberry pie was unique since it was not the usual crust but used the puff pastry mix and well balanced with their scoop of home made ice cream.

We were kind of not sure of going there since we had no reservation and walkin required 45 minute due to today being Friday but we are so glad we went. It was well worth the wait and rewarding.

Walked in on a Saturday evening hoping to get a table for two and were initially told there would be a two-hour wait. We decided to check the bar area and, after about 15 minutes, were able to grab a table there instead.

Overall, the food was good, though I enjoyed some dishes more than others. The short rib quesadilla (6/10) was my least favorite — it was quite greasy and lacked flavor. The tostada de tinga (8/10) was much better: very flavorful and well-balanced. The queso flameado (7/10) was also tasty and came in a generous portion. The churros were the highlight of the meal (9/10) — absolutely delicious.

I’d definitely recommend making a reservation next time to avoid the long wait, but overall it was a solid dining experience.

We tried the esquites, which had a nice char and a little kick. The tostada with pickled carrots was fresh and flavorful, but the blue corn pancakes were definitely the highlight of the meal. Drinks were just okay.

Overall, great ambiance and a really nice spot for brunch, especially if you can get patio seating. Definitely recommend making reservations.

text.text: Came for happy hour on a Monday at the bar with a friend and it was such a cozy and wonderful experience. Neha was our server and was extremely attentive and friendly! For food, I highly recommend the queso and the green beans(the dip surrounding the green beans was so zesty and had amazing umami)!! Don’t skip. For a cocktail, I had the Alma Blanca and it was perfect. It was sweet and spicy at the same time (so a great balance) and so smooth. Every detail, even the candle lit in the bathroom which smells amazing, created a comforting experience.

Great brunch at La Condesa! We arrived right at opening and the service was fast, friendly, and very knowledgeable. The chicken chilaquiles, huevos rancheros, churro waffles,  and queso flameado were all hot, fresh, and full of flavor.

Agua Frescas were super tasty and refreshing.

They were very accommodating about us not eating pork and the brunch menu is surprisingly vegetarian‑friendly. Do note that the queso is authentic Mexican queso (not Tex‑Mex), rich and delicious. So if your expecting Tex-Mex, it may not be for you, but we thought it was delicious.
Eggs were cooked perfectly, and the chilaquiles had some good spiciness but was a bit salty, however it was still excellent.

Generous portions, great quality, and overall a fantastic experience. Highly recommend.

Lastly I had the chicken A la Brasa which came on a bed of sweet potato purée and covered with a chermoula.  The chicken was smoked and came with homemade tortillas (5/5).  Very delicious.
Daniel, my waiter was great.  Very good service.

text.text:
Comedor continues to be one of our favorite dining experiences in Austin. The food is incredible—thoughtful, creative, and full of flavor without ever feeling overcomplicated. Every dish feels intentional, highlighting great ingredients and letting them shine naturally.

What really stood out on our visit was the hospitality from the bar team. They was welcoming, knowledgeable, and genuinely cared about making our experience special. From their cocktail recommendations to the overall service, everything felt effortless and authentic. You can tell there's a strong culture of hospitality here, and it really elevate an already amazing meal.

Great food is easy to find in Austin. Great food paired with service that makes you want to come back is much harder to find. Comedor delivers both every time.

Went for a birthday celebration. Our server Jason was really good. Most of us were vegetarians and he walked us through the menu with patience. It was packed for a Friday evening. We had reservations and got a nice booth. I wouldn’t have liked the tables , for the shear number of people. We all ordered a drink and a plate. None of us paid less than $80 each. There is tax and then there was hospitality tax and also tip 25% (which I gave) I think food was $40 but tax and tip was another $40. Our friend returned her enchiladas. It was stuffed with 100% carrot bites. The quesadilla was very bland, thank goodness for the spicy sauce.

I really think they could have upped their menu with zucchini, broccoli, avocados or asparagus offering.

Overall happy with the ambience. Food not good, parking is paid and all the tip and taxes ruined it for us.

text.text:
We’ve had our eyes on Bill’s Oyster for a long time, and we’re happy to report they are absolutely worth the hype everyone talks about! We originally knew them for their insanely fresh seafood (and yes, it really is that fresh), but what we weren’t expecting was how incredible their brunch would be!

From the moment we walked in, our host Aubrey set the tone. He was incredibly attentive, knowledgeable, and friendly, exactly the kind of person you want guiding you through a menu full of heavy hitters and what feels like big decisions in the moment!

We made reservations ahead of time since the space is on the smaller side and wanted to ensure we get an inside spot since we were celebrating our anniversary. It wasn’t packed when we arrived, but I’d still recommend booking a reservation just to be safe. They also have a super cute and quaint patio which looks like it would be incredible when the whether cooperates!

Now… the food. We’ve seen and heard lots about their seafood, happy hour and of course their famous burger, but hardly saw anything about brunch so we knew that was what we wanted to hit! Cause we're different like that!

Honestly, brunch is where they surprised us the most. Every single dish was high quality, beautifully executed, and full of flavor!

The oysters, seasonal crudo, and michelada clams (coming from a non michelada person) lived up to their reputation, but the brunch menu? Next level!

We got the Chicken Fried Waygu Steak topped with a crawfish tasso gravy which was large, in charge and incredibly crispy! It was the hubby's fav!

I had my eye on the Johnny Cakes topped with Smoked Salmon and the Banana Foster Stuffed French Toast and YUP, those were the stars for me!

The Johnny Cakes aka basically an incredibly delicious fluffy cornbread muffin felt so light and refreshing paired with their salmon and creme fraiche.

But honestly if you go, you HAVE to try the Bananas Foster stuffed French Toast. (Whether you want it as your main or dessert, not only is the presentation beautiful, the bruleed bananas on top, the luxurious filling, fluffy brioche, everything about it was like heaven sent an angel to my plate) It was hands down one of the best we’ve had in Austin! Absolute must-order!

Drink wise, we're tequila and beer people and absolutely LOVED the Mexican martini! This was my second ever Mexican Martini and I can officially say I might be converted from a margarita lover! Perfectly balanced in flavors, but you might not be walking perfectly balanced after two of them (in the best way of course) haha!

Since we were celebrating our anniversary they even brought us a slice of cheesecake (they made sure to ask if we still had room in the tank) and YUP, also worth it! They even fly it in straight from the bronx! Its like no other cheesecake we've ever had, seriously! If you love cheesecake and you want a taste of the east coast, then you better pull the trigger on this! Eat it there or take it to go, you won't regret it!

Whether you’re here for brunch, seafood, or both, Bill’s delivers on EVERY FRONT! We left full, happy, and already know we need to head back for more! Highly recommend!

text.text: We went to Bar Toti to try their all night happy hour on a Monday and it made for a lovely night! It is a small space, very intimate and cute. We sat outside at first before moving inside because of weather and both areas had a lovely ambiance. About the food - I’ll go into detail about each dish we got and why I gave it 3 stars. The hongos a la plancha comes highly recommended from both reviews and staff, however I wished I had gotten something else after trying it. The mushrooms that we were served were not the meaty, scored ones shown in other photos, ours looked and tasted overcooked and were swimming in oil. I don’t think this dish fit my personal tastes as it was mostly just very oily and rich, so if you also dislike those flavors, I don’t recommend it. Also, the burger didn’t live up to the hype for me, as I had heard it was one of the best smash burgers in town and it unfortunately was not a standout to me. I appreciate its uniqueness and the happy hour deal, but it was not exactly well executed - the bun took up most of my bites, it had an overpowering mustard flavor, and I could barely taste the ham. I’ll give them the benefit of the doubt because many other reviews rave about these dishes, so they could’ve just had an off night! We ordered the fries and the focaccia as well, both were good and the focaccia was beautiful but over-salted. The overall flavors of the menu are along the lines of these dishes, quite salty & oily with not much freshness or bright flavors. I’m hoping I’m the exception, but the food wasn’t amazing to me. The service was wonderful, all the staff are very accommodating and friendly! Special thank you to Steven, he was a great server.

We ordered the lobster rolls and crab cake. I'd say the lobster roll was decent but not spectacular. I prefer main style lobster rolls which has mayo and celery. Connecticut lobster rolls are also popular which is mostly butter. Clark's lobster roll combines both styles and i felt it overpowered the lobster. The lobster was high quality and fresh and I liked the roll it was served on. They do not offer gluten free bread options. I have a love-hate relationship with their fries, I love shoe string fries but they are really hard to eat and it is awkward to eat them in a nicer dining setting. Thr crab cake was entirely crab and i could not taste any breading, no complaints there. I would much rather get a lobster roll from here where in a elevated ambiance than a food truck, especially when the price difference is miniminal.

A major negative is that the lettuce the lobster was served on was not washed properly, it has dirt on it.

Dinner at Clark’s last night and it absolutely delivered.

The lobster roll was excellent and the oysters were delicious — we had a mix from New Brunswick and Massachusetts that were fresh and briny in the best way. The real surprise of the night was the ceviche, which might honestly be the best I’ve ever had.

Around the table, the burger got rave reviews, the crispy salmon with polenta was really good, and the linguini with clams was a big hit as well.

Drinks were great too — a crisp local pilsner from Meanwhile Brewing and a fantastic mocktail.

Add in wonderful service and the whole experience felt relaxed, polished, and genuinely enjoyable. A great night out all around.

text.text:
Odd Duck in Austin absolutely lives up to the hype.

From the second you walk in, the place has that perfect Austin energy. It feels upscale without being stiff, creative without trying too hard, and lively without being overwhelming. The atmosphere is warm, fun, and just cool enough to make you feel like you picked the right spot before the food even hits the table.

The staff was amazing from start to finish. Everyone we interacted with was kind, friendly, and genuinely welcoming. Not the fake polite kind of service either. The real kind. The kind where people seem like they actually enjoy being there and want you to enjoy being there too. That makes a huge difference, especially at a restaurant with food this good. Now the food. Top tier is the only way to put it.

I had the wagyu burger, and I am not exaggerating when I say it was life changing. Perfectly cooked, rich, juicy, layered with flavor, and somehow both elevated and comforting at the same time. Every bite tasted intentional. The bun, the patty, the crunch, the greens, the sauce, everything worked together like it had been engineered by someone who takes burgers way more seriously than most people take their careers. It was one of those meals where you take the first bite and immediately stop talking for a second because your brain needs to catch up.

Odd Duck is the kind of restaurant that makes dinner feel like an experience instead of just a meal. Great atmosphere, incredible service, and food that absolutely earns the reputation. Whether you’re visiting Austin or you live here and somehow haven’t gone yet, Odd Duck needs to be on your list.

I’ll definitely be back. And yes, I’ll probably be thinking about that wagyu burger until then. As well as how awesome Jason was and singing Little Mermaid at the bar with him!

Carve  is a beautiful restaurant, and I had heard so many great things about it. My son and my husband both had wonderful experiences here in the past, so I was really excited to finally try it. I made a reservation for Thanksgiving, but unfortunately my experience didn’t live up to the expectations.

I ordered the Thanksgiving turkey special. The turkey itself had good flavor maybe just a little drybut our server kindly brought extra gravy when I asked, and that did help. The mashed potatoes were delicious. However, the green beans had sliced almonds that tasted rancid, which made that side unpleasant.

The meal also came with a salad option (walnuts and apples), and I found it disappointing. It lacked dressing, had too many walnuts, and barely any apple. It just wasn’t enjoyable; I probably should have chosen the soup instead.

We also ordered the artichoke dip, which I personally didn’t like at all—I’ve had much better elsewhere. My daughter ordered the prosciutto and fig pizza and didn’t enjoy it either. On the positive side, my husband’s prime rib was very good.

Overall, the Thanksgiving dinner felt underwhelming, especially considering how many people around us were leaving most of their turkey plates unfinished as well. The stuffing wasn’t good, though the turkey itself was fine.

The restaurant is undeniably pretty and has a great atmosphere, and I do want to highlight that our server (in the bar area) was incredibly attentive and kind. The service was excellent.

However, based on the food we had last night, I’m not sure if I would return.

I was really looking forward to going to Uchi today, but unfortunately the experience didn’t meet my expectations. It was my first time visiting, and we chose it to celebrate our anniversary. My boyfriend had been there once before, so we were expecting a great experience—especially since Uchi is such a popular Japanese restaurant in the Austin area.
We went during happy hour and ordered from the happy hour menu. The first two dishes were good, but not amazing. Toward the end, we tried a large fried ball filled with rice, and it tasted very bland and boring.
Overall, the food seemed either under-seasoned or over-seasoned. Some dishes lacked flavor, while others were extremely salty—especially the skewer we ordered, which had far too much salt.
The service also felt very rushed. At one point, our server accidentally knocked over our beer and soy sauce while cleaning the table. As someone who has worked part-time in the service industry, I understand that accidents happen, but usually a small complimentary item or gesture is offered as an apology. Unfortunately, that didn’t happen.
The atmosphere was fine, but not particularly memorable. Given the restaurant’s reputation, I was hoping for a much better overall experience. I do hope they consider updating or improving the menu in the future

I’ve been a regular at Uchi for about a decade, and it’s a place I keep coming back to for good reason. The menu is both diverse and dynamic, there are favorite dishes I revisit every time, along with new offerings that keep things interesting.

The food and service are consistently excellent. Uchi offers a contemporary take on Japanese cuisine, shaped by the vision of James Beard Award–winning chef Tyson Cole in Austin, Texas. The restaurant is always bustling and typically fully booked, drawing a mix of loyal locals, out-of-town visitors, and even Japanese tourists.

It’s a standout dining experience that has maintained its quality and creativity over the years.

We chose the omakase-style tasting menu and a few à la carte, and every single dish was truly delicious—there wasn’t one course we didn’t enjoy. The quality of the food was exceptional and clearly reflects a high level of culinary skill.

The only critique I would offer is the pacing of the experience. At times, the courses felt rushed. On a few occasions, additional dishes were plated before we had finished the previous course, or food arrived and sat briefly, affecting the intended temperature. Where we were sitting in the middle of the dining room, the servers would rush by adding to the “rush” feel. I think everyone needs to slow down a bit and just enjoy. Given the level of craftsmanship involved, a slower, more intentional pace would allow each dish to be appreciated fully.

The servers were attentive and professional, though it was evident they were very busy. Menu descriptions were delivered quite quickly, which added to the overall feeling of being rushed. Slowing down slightly—both in service and explanation—would elevate the experience even further.

Overall, the food itself was outstanding, and with a more relaxed, deliberate flow, this restaurant could offer an even more memorable and immersive dining experience.

For our appetizer, we ordered the spinach dip. It was probably the best I've had anywhere. It was very flavorful and it was hard to stop eating it. I also had to order their signature French dip with prime rib. It was phenomenal. I had no chewy pieces of meat, it was very juicy and the soft warm bun was chef's kiss. The shoestring fries were seasoned perfectly and the coleslaw was also delicious with their homemade dressing. As for dessert, we couldn't pass up their key lime pie. It was topped with some homemade whip cream and the crust had a hint of cinnamon in the graham cracker crust. It wasn't overly sweet or too heavy like a cheesecake. We definitely look forward to coming back again soon, because every dish was just top notch.

text.text:
This was my first time visiting Bartlett’s, and I was genuinely excited to try it after hearing good things. We ordered steak, kids’ meals, and the French dip sandwich—food-wise, everything was fine and met expectations.

Unfortunately, the service issue completely overshadowed the experience. My raspberry lemonade arrived with a fly/bug in it. When I brought it to our server, Preston, there was no acknowledgment of how unpleasant or unsanitary that was. He simply took the drink away, acted like it wasn’t a big deal, that was it— no comfort/hospitality check in. Probably mixed in the ice, but still…

I wasn’t looking for a discount, a free item, or any kind of compensation. What I was expecting was basic hospitality: an apology, reassurance, or even a small gesture of accountability. The drink wasn’t even removed from the bill, which was disappointing and avoidable.

Bartlett’s has the potential to be great, but moments like this are where service really matters. A little care, professionalism, and empathy would have gone a long way and completely changed how I felt leaving the restaurant.

text.text: We absolutely loved our dinner for three and were shocked we had not discovered Bartlett’s before. We enjoyed creative and delicious cocktails, we all loved the Bartlett Pear Cocktail and our second two were excellent as well! We paired these with roasted artichokes which were excellent and another signature appetizer. We told our waiter he was one of the best we had enjoyed in 24 years in Austin. We came for the prime rib for my husband but also enjoyed the aged rib eye and New York strip…both delicious. It was a delight to order wine with the sommelier who took his time and shared his knowledge. Together we shared a key lime pie enjoyed by all. We loved our seating on the balcony and while the restaurant was bustling on a Thursday evening the ambience is calibrated so it didn’t feel noisy and we could treasure our little celebration. We can’t wait to return!

Best meal of the Austin trip: upscale tacos and housemade masa in a welcoming space.

Food: 5 Service: 4.5 Atmosphere: 5
Cost to worth it rating: 3
Opentableable: yes
Return worthiness: yes

Highlights:
- Waitress Kelly was wonderful and so professional. She noticed I was ordering dairy items on side and asked about if pesto in guacamole  was ok. So astute and kind of her. Also on my friends second drink remembered she didn't want salt or her rim without even asking
- Everything tasted so fresh and high quality
- Brisket tacos: packed with flavor--maybe it was the wagyu meat or the black magic oil. Freshly made corn tortillas were awesome. Usually corn ones and pretty throwaway meh, but these added to the greatness of the tacos. 5 stars
- Duck flautas: crispy covered in mild mole. Loved the mashed potato addition inside for some mellowness and texture. 5 stars
- Guacamole: so fresh and that dollop of pesto on top was lovely. Served with crispy masa dippers were impressive almost a 8x11 page size. It was fun to crack off into pieces, but hard to stop eating it. 5 stars
- Sweet potato: friend loved these long charred wedges. 4.5 stars
- Cocktails were stellar. I got the Don Dario which was a play on a marg and delightful
- $12 of a few drinks during lucky hour (Mon-Fri 5-6pm, Sat-Sun 3-5pm)
- High energy vibes in a clean, open, tan colored space
- Had their bottle water on the table in a champagne bottle which speaks to my heart

Midlights:
- In East Austin so have to Uber if you are staying more central
- Tacos come in orders of 4. Wish it was less so we could've tried more variety.

Lowlights
- No food discounts for lucky hour
- Didn't have time to try the choco taco which looked amaze
- Large gap of time between items first few items coming out and the rest
