text.text:
La Piscina, located in the beautiful and eclectic Austin Proper Hotel, offers a stunning rooftop setting that makes for a memorable brunch experience. Our group of four was seated on their patio, which was both picturesque and comfortable in temperature.

We were welcomed with freshly made tortilla chips and two house salsas, which set a strong first impression. The cocktails were equally impressive - creative, well-balanced, and beautifully presented. That said, service was inconsistent. It took about 20 minutes to receive our drinks after ordering them, and after they arrived, we didn’t see our server again for another 20 minutes. As a result, we didn’t place our food order until roughly 45 minutes after being seated. It seemed like our server may have been having an off day.

Once ordered, the food arrived promptly and it absolutely delivered. While La Piscina is known for its sizzling fajitas (which we’d definitely recommend), the standout for us was the gulf snapper aguachile -- savory, bright, and incredibly refreshing. The pastry basket was another highlight, with baked goods that were moist and just the right level of sweet.

A couple of notes for future diners: table space on the patio tables is fairly tight, especially when sharing dishes like fajitas, which made things feel a bit cramped. Additionally, despite the hotel’s website noting a partnership with MML Hospitality, MML gift cards are no longer accepted. We had called ahead to confirm and were still surprised to learn this upon trying to pay our bill.

Overall, La Piscina shines in ambiance and food quality, but the service and a few logistical details left room for improvement.

This is a spot I lusted after for a very long time and never tried while living in Austin, so when the opportunity came to try during a recent visit I was so excited and F+D delivered the experience I was craving and then some:)

Our server Kunika was so genuinely friendly and conversational, she gave us some great recommendations for wine to pair with the $1 East Coast oyster special (we went for a salt-forward white), and was so present and attentive! All other servers we interacted with were on the same wavelength, making for the most pleasant service experience!

We paired the oysters with Crispy Fingerlings, Gruyere Popovers, Parisian Gnocchi, and Melted Leek Risotto. All of which were exactly what you’d expect, absolutely phenomenal. The popovers and fingerlings were yummy and complexly savory little accoutrements, while both the gnocchi and risotto were absolutely melt in your mouth umami takes on pasta dishes

F+D is so worth the splurge, I can’t believe I waited so long to try!

text.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ A Standout Sushi Experience

I had an exceptional meal at Neighborhood Sushi. The variety and execution of the dishes made it clear this place takes its craft seriously. We ordered a wide range of items, and not a single plate missed.

The Secret Garden and To Saturn and Back were creative, balanced, and beautifully presented. The Broccolini Tempura and Truffled Beech Mushroom Tempura hit that perfect light-crispy texture without feeling heavy, and the Corn Kakiage was surprisingly addictive.

Nigiri was the real highlight. The Sea Bream, Tasmanian Trout, Fluke, Japanese Western, and 2 King Crab Nigiri were all incredibly fresh, expertly cut, and seasoned with just the right touch—no soy sauce needed. Even the house-made Kizami Wasabi stood out.

The hot items were equally strong: the Basil Shrimp Tempura was delicate and flavorful, the Amberjack Crudo was bright and clean, and the Fish Collar was rich, tender, and perfectly charred.

Cocktails were thoughtful as well—The Rising Sun and Red Dragon Cocktail both paired perfectly with the food without overpowering it.

Service from Tomas was smooth and attentive throughout, and the whole experience felt relaxed but elevated. With the amount and quality of food we ordered, the value felt absolutely justified.

If you want sushi that’s both creative and technically precise, this place is a must. I’d come back in a heartbeat.

Overall this was a good meal, priced as expected for a hotel, but still very good.

The menu is thoughtful and well designed, with dishes that feel intentional and balanced rather than overly complicated. Everything we ordered was beautifully prepared and full of flavor.

If you’re looking for a great dinner spot in Austin with excellent cocktails and a well-crafted menu, this place is an easy recommendation. Totally recommend.

text.text:
Beautiful spot with excellent greens. The Caesar salad is enough for four people. It's a good level of salty and umami. The salty comes from the cheese and the umami from the egg, so there's no sardines and it is vegetarian. The charred cabbage had good moistness with the sauce reaching the core. This is also for four people so make sure to order wisely portion-wise.

The short rib was good and tender. The crudo you should make sure to have a piece of fur with each piece of fish so that the acid makes the tiger's milk pop better.

The atmosphere is lovely, either for a date night or a big get-together. Definitely a memorable place to visit with excellent staff.

Great fine dining restaurant in the heart of Austin. The presentation of dishes is very good and their service is top notch. Every dish was carefully crafted with great attention to detail and was served really well by their staff. The vibe/atmosphere is very pleasant and not too loud.
Halibut is a must try - the taste is really balanced and the sauce that accompanies the fish is really good.

text.text:
Dined solo at Hestia for my solo pre-Valentine's date and was impressed by both the food and the precision of service.

I was seated with a clear view of the dining room and could see how smoothly the team operated. Service was coordinated, attentive, and never intrusive. My water glass was consistently refilled before it reached half.

As a solo diner, I especially appreciated the attention to detail. The table was fully and intentionally set from the start, no last-minute adjustments or removed place settings. It may seem small, but it makes a difference.

The food was excellent and thoughtfully executed. The scallops were the standout — perfectly cooked, rich, and balanced. Definitely pick up the shell and drink the tallow after!

For the quality of ingredients, technique, and service, the value felt appropriate.

Hestia delivers polished service, strong execution, and a dining experience that feels deliberate at every level.

text.text:
Review: Heatia  Cozy Luxury with Hits and Misses
Visited Heatia last Saturday. The overall ambiance is cozy yet luxurious, making it a perfect spot for dinner. Even though it was a busy Saturday night, the staff managed everything quite well, and the food was served surprisingly fast.

Here’s a breakdown of the dishes I tried:
🤍 The Highlights (Must-Orders!)
• Caviar Tart: Absolute perfection! This was incredibly delicious. The chef did an amazing job balancing all the flavors beautifully. Highly recommended!
• Scallops: Perfectly executed. The scallops were beautifully tender and cooked just right.
• Yuzu Orange Shaved Ice: A fantastic dessert to end the meal. It was delicious, refreshing, and the perfect palate cleanser.
💬 The Average / Not For Me
• Tuna Crudo: This was alright, but the tuna was very lean. I personally prefer fattier fish, so this particular dish didn't really hit the spot for me. (If you prefer lean fish, you might like it!)
• Wagyu Tartare: I found the beef aroma/gamey scent to be a bit too strong for my liking.
• Halibut: The fish itself was cooked beautifully—not overcooked at all and still juicy. However, the sauce was unfortunately a bit too salty.
Overall:
A great restaurant with a lovely atmosphere and solid service, even during the weekend rush. The Caviar Tart and the dessert were the stars of the night. For the mains, it really comes down to personal preference regarding texture and flavor profiles. Definitely worth a visit!

text.text:
We visited this fine-dining restaurant, and unfortunately, the experience was quite mixed. Here is my detailed impression of the dishes and the service.
Food:
Oysters. They were very fresh, with a creative and visually appealing presentation. However, the non-classic sauces didn’t work for me — traditional pairings would have tasted better.
Steak tartare. A complete disappointment. You can barely taste the meat: the pieces are tiny and thin, and the flavor is completely overpowered by a grain that tastes like toasted buckwheat.
Mushrooms. Over-seasoned and over-fried. They were meant to be piquant, but there were so many spices that you could literally feel the powdery texture.
Halibut. The highlight of the entire evening was perfectly cooked, beautifully presented, and incredibly delicious. The only dish I would genuinely want to order again.
Desserts (panna cotta and ice cream). Both desserts were interesting, but the ice cream was the clear winner.
Atmosphere:
There is a powerful smell of smoke inside — so strong that your hair and clothes end up absorbing it completely. This was highly unpleasant.
Service:
Even though there were free tables and we had a reservation, we waited about 20 minutes before being seated. The waitress taking our order was very polite and knowledgeable about the menu, but the staff bringing out the dishes mixed up where to place them.
We were also celebrating two birthdays, and the situation with the desserts was uncomfortable: we ordered two desserts, but both received candles. The second one was placed in front of the other birthday person, who didn’t even order a dessert. It felt awkward and unprofessional. In restaurants of this level, it's standard to offer a complimentary dessert for birthday guests, but here everything felt strange and poorly handled.
Overall:
I’m giving one star for the halibut and one star for the waitress.
Unfortunately, the restaurant doesn’t deserve more than that. I would not return.

text.text: Excellent food, cocktails, atmosphere, and service. It’s not hard to see why it’s on the Michelin guide. We visited with two toddlers early on a Saturday evening and were treated very well. It wasn’t quite busy nor very loud at that point, so it worked well. The drinks were creative and delicious. Lovely plating for each of the dishes, and everything was served at a perfect temperature. They even had a well-lit single bathroom with a lovely changing table available, which I didn’t expect but certainly appreciated. The staff were all very kind and accommodating, and the service was fast and efficient. Drinks from the bar came quickly and looked as good as they tasted. Portions were quite large for the price and quality level in my opinion. The steak dish and ceviche in particular felt quite generously sized — certainly enough for two to four to share if you’re eating family-style. We ordered three appetizers / tapas and one “main” and could barely finish.

Found this place on Instagram and was excited to try it, especially since it’s a Michelin Guide restaurant. After eating here, I’m not entirely sure what Michelin was tasting.

The whole experience felt a little confusing. I couldn’t quite figure out what vibe they were going for, and unfortunately the food didn’t help. To make matters worse, a “glitch” caused every table seated after us to get their food before we did.

When the food finally arrived, it was a letdown. My boyfriend’s $50 chicken was dry, and my seafood dish looked like an aquarium explosion on top of green mystery paste. The presentation was so confusing I thought the fish was bread.

The drinks were fine, but between the service, atmosphere, and food, this one missed the mark. Michelin Guide 2025? That’s the most surprising thing on the menu.

text.text:
My husband and I enjoyed an Anniversary Dinner at Olamaie. A short summary would be "Great Food, but way too expensive for the performance". We are blessed to have dined internationally in all kinds of elevated and Michelin Star rated restaurants for the past decade. Olamaie has for sure good food but could be categorized as an elevated bistro, instead a Michelin Star Restaurant. We enjoyed the Prix Fixe Menu with one of us eating meat and one veggie option. While the food overall was innovative and very tasty, the Velvet Brownie Dessert was very disappointing. This was grocery store standard.
But from the start: We were greeted friendly and every server seemed to know that it was our anniversary. We even got a sweet anniversary card. We would have wished for the same attention to detail during our visit, as we were not offered any additional drinks in between our meal. Opportunity clearly missed here. Our server was friendly, although she seems to be very bored at her job. The best dish of the menu was for sure the Cauliflower in a very tasty espuma! Very well done! And as expected, the highly rated biscuits were absolute outstanding. Excellent! Unfortunately, we were relatively rushed through our evening, as the next course was almost served immediately after clearing the previous course. This was a bummer. The next bummer was the price point. While knowing that the Menu was $175 per person, we paid over $500 for two menus, two glasses of Champagne and one cocktail. (We were not offered any additional beverages after the server cleared the empty glasses - another opportunity missed to create an attentive guest experience). My husband and I enjoyed an Anniversary Dinner at Olamaie. A short summary would be "Great Food, but way too expensive for the performance". We are blessed to have dined internationally in all kinds of elevated and Michelin Star rated restaurants for the past decade. Olamaie has for sure good food but could be categorized as an elevated bistro, instead a Michelin Star Restaurant. We enjoyed the Prix Fixe Menu with one of us eating meat and one veggie option. While the food overall was innovative and very tasty, the Velvet Brownie Dessert was very disappointing. This was grocery store standard.
But from the start: We were greeted friendly and every server seemed to know that it was our anniversary. We even got a sweet anniversary card. We would have wished for the same attention to detail during our visit, as we were not offered any additional drinks in between our meal. Opportunity clearly missed here. Our server was friendly, although she seems to be very bored at her job. The best dish of the menu was for sure the Cauliflower in a very tasty espuma! Very well done! And as expected, the highly rated biscuits were absolute outstanding. Excellent! Unfortunately, we were relatively rushed through our evening, as the next course was almost served immediately after clearing the previous course. This was a bummer. Lutie’s is a wonderful choice for a romantic dinner, with incredible service, exquisite food, and a truly special ambiance. Highly recommended.

I had a wonderful dinner at Lutie’s and overall it was such a memorable experience. The food was absolutely incredible. Everything we ordered was cooked to perfection. The scallops & chickpeas were phenomenal, the quail was delicious, and the barbecue lobster was flavorful and perfectly cooked. Even the sourdough bread was stand-out good!

Our server was very knowledgeable about the menu and gave fantastic recommendations, which really elevated the meal. That said, service did feel a bit on the slower side at times, likely because she had quite a few tables to manage. I could tell she was doing her best and handled it gracefully.

The restaurant itself is stunning! So much charm and attention to detail in the design. My only small suggestion would be to adjust the temperature inside, as it felt quite cold and even other guests nearby seemed to notice.

Overall, I’d highly recommend Lutie’s for a special night out; the food alone makes it worth it, and with a few small tweaks, it could be truly flawless.

text.text:
An absolute brunch masterpiece!
If you’re looking for the best brunch spot in Austin, Poeta is it. I’m already counting down the days until I can go back!

From the second we walked in, the vibes were perfect. The entire staff were incredibly friendly and attentive—they truly make you feel welcome, especially the bartender Kat, crafting the best drinks. And the food? Everything was so delicious!
Here’s the breakdown of what blew us away:
• The Kolaches: You can tell these are freshly baked. They were pillowy, warm, and easily some of the best I've had.
• The Avocado Toast: This is a bold claim, but it’s the best avocado toast I’ve ever had. They do a white bean purée with whole white beans on top that adds such a sophisticated, creamy texture.
• The Breakfast Plate: Every bite was a powerhouse of flavor. It’s a classic dish elevated with so many unique notes.
• The Hash Browns: Forget everything you know about standard hash browns. These were ultra-crispy with a unique spin that made them addictive.
• Waffle with Gelato: We ended with the waffle, which came topped with gelato and a buttery espresso syrup. It was such a unique, yummy combination of flavors that I haven't seen anywhere else.
Poeta isn’t just a meal; it’s an experience. Amazing service, creative dishes, and top-tier flavors. See you guys again very soon!

text.text:
We chose Juniper for the first time to celebrate my birthday and were excited to finally try it. Overall, the food was excellent and we truly enjoyed our meal, but the service left us feeling disappointed.

We started with the focaccia with whipped ricotta and the piquillo peppers, both of which were delicious. For our entrees, we ordered the cacio e pepe and the rigatoni alla vodka, and both pasta dishes were flavorful and well executed. The food was easily the highlight of the evening.

Unfortunately, the service did not match the quality of the meal. Our waiter was adequate, but he never made the experience feel special, especially considering we were there celebrating a birthday. Throughout the evening, he seemed somewhat annoyed to be serving our table, though we initially brushed it off.

After placing our full order, we received our appetizers at 7:26 p.m. and then waited another 33 minutes for our pasta dishes to arrive. While we understand that timing can vary, it was difficult not to notice several nearby tables who ordered after us receiving their meals first. We're not sure what happened, but it left us feeling as though our table had been overlooked.

While we enjoyed the food and are glad we gave Juniper a try, the service ultimately left us hesitant to return.

text.text:
Juniper continues to prove why it’s one of Austin’s premier dining destinations.

We started with the Puffy Potato, topped with pecorino fonduta and white truffle oil, and it was absolutely phenomenal. Rich, indulgent, and packed with flavor.

The Crudo was a standout. The combination of avocado purée, salted cucumber, everything bagel seeds, and finger lime was incredibly fresh and creative. Every bite delivered something different, and honestly, it was one of those dishes that makes you stop and appreciate how good it is.

The Cacio e Pepe was everything you’d hope for—simple, classic, and executed perfectly.

For the main event, the Cavatelli with rock shrimp, vermouth butter, serrano, lemon, and breadcrumbs was pure perfection. The balance of richness, brightness, heat, and texture was spot on.

From start to finish, every dish was thoughtfully prepared and beautifully presented. Juniper delivers elevated Italian-inspired cuisine without feeling pretentious, and it’s easy to see why it’s become such a staple of Austin’s dining scene. Looking forward to my next visit.

Oh I have sooo much to say - ALL GOOD THINGS ❤️

Was here last night to celebrate my husband’s birthday.

We were in the salon area which was pretty private. Tables weren’t packed so even though there were other parties it felt like our own little place.
Our table was ready ahead of time, there was no waiting.
Service was warm. Not overly interfering. There was plenty of help on Menu in case we had questions.

All the courses were served only when the previous ones were finished which is a big plus for me. I hate it when places dump everything on the table all at once.

Martinis were lit. Rigatoni was delicious. And we had stuffed peppers which were just so unique - in a good way.

And here the best part. For desserts we had Milk and Honey. Oh my goodness!!!! If you are there please never skip it. Its sooooooo good. I’d come back here again & again just for that.

It was my husband’s birthday so the dessert was on the house. And we were given a return present as well when we left.

All in all, loved the place, the people, the food. Everything.

Keep up the amazing work guys!!

We had an exceptional experience at Juniper. Our server, Abby, was phenomenal—attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely warm throughout the entire evening. Her service elevated the experience from start to finish.

Overall, this was a fantastic dining experience. Highly recommend, and I’m already looking forward to returning.

We’ve walked by this place so many times…and not until a friend recommended that we try it, did I end up looking at the menu. Let me be that friend for you!
NOT the Tex Mex we expected and as someone that has been to CDMX multiple times, this hit the spot! Only American thing about it is the giant portion sizes!
Their cocktails were delicious and I do love some infused tequila or mezcal drinks for that extra special treatment. Shot out to the Chapulin - watermelon infused mezcal perfection.
We had the esquite (corn) with the bone marrow and OMG - this was the most bone marrow I have EVER been served in a restaurant. Huitlacoche quesadilla was great and the chicken mole huarache - so addictive. The birria though - this was the dish that finally made me understand people’s obsession with a good birria taco. We’ve walked by this place so many times…and not until a friend recommended that we try it, did I end up looking at the menu. Let me be that friend for you!
NOT the Tex Mex we expected and as someone that has been to CDMX multiple times, this hit the spot! Only American thing about it is the giant portion sizes!
Their cocktails were delicious and I do love some infused tequila or mezcal drinks for that extra special treatment. Shot out to the Chapulin - watermelon infused mezcal perfection.
We had the esquite (corn) with the bone marrow and OMG - this was the most bone marrow I have EVER been served in a restaurant. Huitlacoche quesadilla was great and the chicken mole huarache - so addictive. The birria though - this was the dish that finally made me understand people’s obsession with a good birria taco. Perfection!
Our biggest learning from the visit - either bring friends or order less though. Can’t wait to be back!

text.text: Initially, the impression of this establishment was that it would offer a suitable dining experience with satisfactory service. I can confirm that the food was of high quality, with superb taste; however, there should be more generous portion sizes, and if a smaller portion is served, the price should reflect that. Regrettably, the coffee was tasteless and unappealing; I will not be purchasing coffee here again. The staff member serving us displayed a problematic attitude from the beginning, despite our being courteous and not difficult. For example, I requested another coffee due to a sugar stain; although I tried it with regular brown sugar, the taste remained unpleasant—indeed, gross. The server's attitude was unprofessional, characterized by eye-rolling and sighing, as if she were exhausted. At the end of our visit, when we requested separate tickets, she sighed again, implying difficulty in processing the bill. Additionally, she did not check if my companions wished to order more soda. I could have left a generous tip, but her attitude discouraged this. My companions mentioned that this was their first and last visit; they also noted that the waitress at Denny's on Oltorf was more genuine and pleasant. I attempted to contact the manager to report these issues; however, the representative who answered was unwilling to provide her name or the manager’s, and I informed them I would follow up via email.

text.text:
We came into Curra's the Monday after Grand Prix weekend when all restaurants seems overbooked. We were seated immediately for a late lunch around 1-2pm. Staff were very fast and attentive and explained the menu for us.

This was very different than what we're used to with California-Mexican food. The spice level is intense, but we really enjoyed the bright flavors as well. The dishes might have been a tad too spicy for us, and we have decent spice tolerance, but we'd come back just to try more of their menu.

I ordered the patos en mole tacos, and my dad got the cochinita pixel, both so flavorful and satisfying. We would definitely come back.

text.text:
This restaurant is a delicious part of Austin’s history! The building is over a hundred years old and has been home to Cisco’s since 1950.

While I enjoy all of the food, my favorite dish is the chicken fried steak (which reminds me of my mother’s) served with a side of veggies and a delicious biscuit. The biscuits are handmade fresh daily and served all day. You can even get a bag of biscuits to go.

They serve breakfast all day, so go ahead and order pancakes and fajitas! I wish they were open later, a chicken fried steak would be a great way to end a night out on east 6th!

text.text:
Cisco’s Restaurant, Bar & Bakery – East Austin. A true East Austin institution with 75 years of history and family-run charm, Cisco’s definitely earns points for nostalgia and character. The space is tiny but quaint, filled with old-school Tex-Mex vibes that make you feel like you’ve stepped into a slice of Austin’s past.

I ordered the carne guisada and migas tacos with water • both were okay, but lacked the bold flavor I was hoping for. The tortillas weren’t homemade, which surprised me given how long this place has been around. I remember having a similar experience years ago, so maybe I just haven’t found my go-to order here yet.

Parking was a headache; honestly spent more time circling the block than sitting down to eat. That said, the waitress was lovely and attentive, and the festive, colorful interior added a nice touch to the overall experience.

Cisco’s is undeniably cool for its legacy and local roots, but I’d love to see the tortillas elevated to match the heritage. Not sure if I’ll be back, but I respect what they represent in Austin’s food scene.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

text.text:
For how much we ended up spending, the value was not there. The staff were all extremely kind people so this is nothing to do with chosen staff.

I liked the light brightness setting, the pots outside were beautiful and the flooring in the entry stunning.

I understand this was a social environment, city vibes, but the distance between the tables at the wall booth was almost impossible to squeeze in and out of - Really uncomfortable. The menus were beautiful but also uncomfortably large for the table and space.

At this price point, we’re paying for an experience and unmatched flavors. We would have not expected plastic flowers in the presentation and cheap feeling table chargers.
The flavor of the food was fine. It did not have us saying wow or planning a trip back to have anything again.

The cost isn’t the issue, but the value received from it. We came in prepared to spend what we ended up spending, but truthfully we won’t be recommending the restaurant to anyone looking for a special night.

We respect the effort but we’re really disappointed with having spent $400+ on a special night to walk away displeased.

text.text: Had a chance to take some clients out for a post work dinner and chose The Guest House Austin.  Been to the Las Vegas location, which was nice, but this one, just wow!  Wednesday night, 6:15pm reservation, already pretty full.  Chill music playing.  By the time we were finishing our appetizers, they had an in-house DJ spinning some fantastic songs that picked up the vibe perfectly! Get seated, order some appetizers, table is constantly being touched by our servers, Amanda (who was amazing and I highly recommend requesting her if you book a reservation) and the team who made sure drinks were never empty, dishes were constantly swapped out as well as silverware.  Truly an elevated experience.  Amanda did a wonderful job engaging the table, took all of our orders by memory, which is risky but she did not make a single mistake.  I asked her about it and she said it allowed her to stay engaged with the guests.  Top notch!  Everything she recommended was exactly as she described.  It's not often you get a meal where every single thing from the bread (almost criminal to call that bread because it was so delicious) to the appetizers (Steak Tartare, Spicy Rigatoni, Beets, Apple & Endive Salad) to the entrees (Rosewood, Cacio e Pepe w/ house made noodles, Short Rib, Veal Parm, Whipped Potatoes, Broccolini) to the drinks (too many to name but we did get one of their Theatrical drinks) and the desserts (Lemon Swirl Cheesecake, S'mores, and Ice Cream Sandwich).  I don't drink and I had mentioned it once at the beginning of our experience to Amanda so when we got a round of champagne to toast, she brought me a non-alcoholic, and with the Theatrical drink, she made sure I wasn't left out and brought me a non-alcoholic serving of Mango Margarita).
